p0_strong_or_canonical.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: mixed-precision attention kernel / long-context inference
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. Existing methods either use a uniform low-precision path or select token interactions, leaving spatial precision routing over hardware-aligned score tiles outside fused dense attention. We introduce TileMix, a tile-centric precision-routing kernel that makes numerical precision an executable spatial decision over score-tile groups within fused dense attention. TileMix partitions the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles, packs routing decisions into compact bitmasks, and dispatches each tile group through FP16 or INT8 score computation while both paths update a shared online-softmax state. Scalable precision grouping lets each routing bit govern multiple adjacent key tiles, preserving hardware-aligned compute tiles and compact metadata at long contexts. By routing all legal tile groups, TileMix preserves dense token connectivity, requires no training, and supports grouped-query attention, variable-length batches, and INT8 key/value caches. Across LongEval, LV-Eval, and A100 prefill benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna, TileMix recovers long-context quality lost under uniform INT8 and improves prefill throughput over FP16, yielding a controllable accuracy-efficiency frontier across model families. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: Global Simulation-Guided Dynamic Operator Scheduling for Efficient Multi-Tenant Model Serving
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: multi-tenant model serving / operator-level scheduling
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Container-granularity scheduling leaves abundant short-lived idle slices within containers unexploited. Reallocating containers is too heavyweight to utilize such fine-grained opportunities under SLA constraints, and operator-level scheduling requires reasoning about dependencies, memory safety, and cluster-wide execution dynamics in real time. In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: KV-cache paging / multi-agent serving
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Production paged-serving engines apply uniform paging granularity to the KV cache, even though the two regions of a multi-agent workload have opposite storage requirements: a long shared prefix demands contiguity, while the per-request suffix demands fine-grained allocation. We present \textbf{GraniKV}, a KV-cache layer that allocates the shared prefix in a contiguous HOT pool and the suffix in a token-level COLD pool, combined with a per-step dispatcher which selects the appropriate backend among dual backends for each regime (compute-, memory-, or communication-bound). To the best of our knowledge, GraniKV is the first system to apply asymmetric paging granularity to the KV cache of a production paged-serving engine. At $L_p{=}16$\,K shared tokens GraniKV reaches $\mathbf{2.16\times}$, $\mathbf{1.98\times}$, and $\mathbf{1.57\times}$ output-token throughput over the production baseline on Llama-3.1-8B/TP=1, Qwen-2.5-14B/TP=2, and Qwen-2.5-32B/TP=4. The gain decomposes: cascade attention integration contributes the majority at saturation; the asymmetric storage layer adds $1.05$--$1.15\times$ end-to-end while being what makes the batched-GEMM prefix backend possible at all. Under heterogeneous multi-agent serving with \emph{distinct} prompts of different lengths, the attribution inverts: GraniKV sustains $\mathbf{1.95\times}$ while batch-global cascade collapses to parity --- the storage layer alone carries the win in the regime that motivates the paper.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: VLA device-edge co-inference / energy-aware runtime
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. Thus, we propose EcoVLA, an adaptive device-edge co-inference framework for VLA models that maximizes system energy efficiency under real-time constraints. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: MoE memory-efficient W4A16 inference / GPU slot cache
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models reduce arithmetic by activating only a small subset of experts per token, yet deployment still requires storing and moving the full expert bank. We present ExactMoE, an inference design that applies symmetric group-128 four-bit weight quantization only to routed experts, stores those experts in kernel-native MARLIN form in pinned host memory, and executes all selected experts through a configurable GPU-resident slot cache and fused grouped MoE kernels. The router, attention, embeddings, normalization layers, and language-model head remain in BF16. "Exact" refers to complete expert availability and an unchanged top-k routing procedure: no expert is pruned, substituted, or forced to execute on the CPU. It does not imply numerical identity with the BF16 model. On OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, evaluated on a single NVIDIA L4, a 16-slot configuration reduces peak reserved GPU memory from 14.168 to 1.836 GiB (87.04%) while retaining 81.85% of BF16 decode throughput. A fully resident 64-slot configuration reaches 31.923 tokens/s versus 21.662 tokens/s for BF16 while reserving 4.061 GiB. Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. In a matched 16-token ablation, fused grouped execution is 1.97x as fast as a sequential W4 reference. These results identify a practical memory-transfer-throughput frontier for complete-expert MoE inference.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: MoE expert-parallel load balancing / serving
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: In expert-parallel (EP) MoE serving, every layer synchronizes at the slowest GPU. Dispatchers balance token counts (EPLB, LPLB, UltraEP) or activated-expert counts (METRO), assuming expert time is linear in one. Measurements on two datacenter GPU generations show it is neither: below $n^* \approx 156$--$168$ tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates---cost attaches to $activated replicas$, not tokens; above it, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile $M$-tiles, so $splitting$ an expert adds padded compute. A max-affine profile $t=\max(a+bG,\,c+βN)$ captures both regimes. Realistic decode batches hold hot experts in the linear regime and cold in the flat $simultaneously$; recorded batches show proxy dispatches differ by $1.4$--$1.6\times$ in modeled block time (p95 up to $1.7\times$), and $which$ proxy wins flips with the regime. We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. Anchored by an 8-GPU Testbed A microbenchmark, TEMPO stays within $1\%$ of the best fixed baseline everywhere and wins by up to $15.5\%$ where regimes mix. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: sparse video attention / DiT inference
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: diffusion cache policy / video-image generation acceleration
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Diffusion models have achieved dominant performance in visual generation but suffer from substantial inference overhead. While cache-based acceleration has emerged as a promising solution, existing policies rely on local similarity heuristics, which we identify as being significantly misaligned with final generation quality. This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: agentic serving characterization / systems benchmark
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Agentic applications are shifting AI serving from isolated model inference to long-running workloads in which LLMs coordinate tools, environments, and persistent state. However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

Moreover, we design customized two-stage routing strategy for DeaMoE to avoid redundant loading, under which DeaMoE greatly improves the efficiency during LLM decoding. Compared with vanilla MoE, DeaMoE reduces per-step loaded weights by up to 50.9% and achieves up to 1.33 end-to-end TPOT speedup for the pre-trained 7B model on A40, and up to 2.00x and 1.97x peak speedup for DeepSeek-V3 on A40 and H100 in microbenchmarks.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
p0_strong_or_canonical.topic: MoE serving / high-bandwidth flash architecture
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

p1_watchlist.why: Show-Harness exposes compact semantic action units with embodiment-specific deterministic interpreters, allowing frontier VLMs to control robots zero-shot and small open VLMs to adapt with only a few GPU-hours. It generalizes across tasks and embodiments without added model capacity or costly embodiment-specific pretraining, but lacks direct serving latency/throughput measurements, so it remains protected Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: PASCAL: A Phase-Aware Shared-Cache Model for Parallel Scans
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / cache modeling / AI accelerators
p1_watchlist.why: Models progress divergence across multicore parallel scans such as attention K/V reuse and GEMM panel reuse without requiring target traces or cycle timing. On 60 NVIDIA GB10 configurations it reaches 13.84% MAPE versus 44.79% for TileSight and 54.16% for exact symbolic SDCM. Valuable design-space model, but not itself an acceleration mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / deployment measurement / serving route / precision and harness
p1_watchlist.why: Measures enterprise AI systems at the actual serving-route level rather than advertised model identifier, explicitly binding weights, precision, output contract and harness. The reference protocol covers 128 tasks and 987 assertions and treats route failures as deployment evidence. High-value systems measurement work, but not a new acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / GUI agents / heterogeneous devices / state transfer
p1_watchlist.why: Benchmarks cross-device GUI workflows across Android, Windows and Ubuntu using typed input-output composition and exposes state-transfer and long-horizon coordination failures. Important heterogeneous-agent infrastructure benchmark, but it does not claim a measured inference acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning / agent memory
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free hierarchical-convolution memory shortens sequential segment processing to a logarithmic tree and exposes parallelism across text segments and reasoning threads. It improves RULER HotpotQA/2WikiMultiHopQA over training-free baselines, but the primary evidence gives no measured latency, throughput, or token-cost reduction, so it stays high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / persistent memory / lifecycle management
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces typed memory lifecycle policies for persistent LLM agents. FR-Bank reaches 76.9% on LifecycleBench and 75.2% on LongMemEval-S while avoiding unbounded undifferentiated memory growth; useful agent-memory infrastructure evidence, but no direct latency/throughput reduction is established in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: Towards Scalable and Cost-Efficient Vulnerability Detection: A Study on Automatic Query Generation
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / code agents / cost-efficient static analysis
p1_watchlist.why: Uses LLMs to synthesize reusable CodeQL queries instead of repeatedly scanning repositories with full LLM reasoning; reports 82% average F1 improvement over baseline CodeQL and includes a cost-benefit analysis showing direct full-repository LLM scanning can be computationally and financially expensive. Retained as high-value agentic tooling watch rather than acceleration strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Frequency-Conditioned Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / flow matching / action generation
p1_watchlist.why: FreqFM makes action frequency an explicit conditioning dimension for flow-matching VLA action experts using DCT-space source matching, frequency-balanced objectives, and frequency-scaled guidance. It improves LIBERO-Plus by 9.3 points and also validates on six real-robot tasks, but reports algorithmic task gains rather than serving/runtime efficiency, so it is retained as protected Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / video inference / efficiency survey / canonical lineage
p1_watchlist.why: Recent survey focused specifically on VideoLLM inference-efficiency mechanisms with concrete parameter, FLOP, latency, memory, visual-token, or audio-token reductions. Useful as a canonical map and recall seed across token pruning, temporal sampling, caching, compression, and multimodal serving, but it is a survey rather than a new acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing for Vision Token Pruning in MLLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / vision token pruning / adaptive routing
p1_watchlist.why: VIP-Router selects among pruning strategies per input with only 0.017% trainable backbone-equivalent parameters. It improves average accuracy by 26.9% relative and utility accounting for realized token cost by 22.0% versus the best fixed strategy, but the abstract does not report end-to-end latency or throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Odometer-Agnostic Drift Correction Using OpenStreetMap Lane Geometry
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / localization / lightweight runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Directly aligns short odometry segments to sparse OpenStreetMap lane centerlines for efficient online correction without dense priors, sensor-specific preprocessing or complex matching pipelines.

p1_watchlist.title: On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Model Adaptation, an Effective Paradigm on Low-Quality Multimodal Data
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / distillation / parameter-efficient adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Learns sample-wise distillation targets with a lightweight controller used only during training, preserving the compact student inference architecture and test-time cost while improving base-to-novel and cross-dataset transfer.

p1_watchlist.title: RiLM: Parameter-Efficient Language Modeling via Geodesic Decoding
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compact language models / parameter efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: RiLM removes the conventional output projection by sharing the token embedding geometry for input and geodesic decoding, targeting sub-million-parameter language models for edge deployment. The controlled results are interesting parameter-efficiency evidence, but the work is small-model focused and lacks wall-clock or energy measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal serving / KV cache / token pruning
p1_watchlist.why: TRACE addresses irreversible visual-token admission in long GUI-agent trajectories with query-independent interaction priors, instruction relevance, novelty and coverage repair, plus monotone KV contraction to avoid repeated visual encoding or pruning. It is directly relevant to agent memory/serving efficiency across six GUI benchmarks, but the primary abstract provides no exact latency, memory or throughput reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: KVShareArena: KV-Cache Reuse Across Contexts and Model Checkpoints
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving / benchmark and cost accounting
p1_watchlist.why: KVShareArena benchmarks non-prefix KV-cache reuse across retrieved chunks, multi-agent reports and model checkpoints, explicitly charging compute, memory and per-request latency and separating one-time cache-build cost. It shows position correction is often enough for single-source reuse but multi-source reuse needs partial re-encoding or training, and unrepaired caches can be worse than no cache. High-value systems benchmark, but not itself a new acceleration runtime.

p1_watchlist.title: What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / context compression
p1_watchlist.why: RD-Forget separates a persistent source archive from a query-conditioned answer-time memory view and uses a rate-distortion formulation to construct that view under an explicit memory budget. It directly targets the long-context inefficiency of retaining everything in the prompt while preserving historical access, making it relevant to agent memory serving, though the abstract does not quantify wall-clock or token savings.

p1_watchlist.title: A-JIT: Agentic Just-In-Time Software Construction
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive runtime
p1_watchlist.why: runtime self-specialization architecture for agentic software

p1_watchlist.title: FolDeX: A Physical-World Benchmark for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation of Deformable Objects
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / long-horizon manipulation / deformable objects / real-robot benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a real-robot benchmark for long-horizon deformable manipulation with 2,000+ hours of physical data, 20+ tasks, and 10+ embodiments, explicitly studying reuse of intervention, recovery, cross-task, cross-scene, and cross-embodiment experience. It is a high-value Physical-AI evaluation and data-reuse resource, not an inference acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: $Φ$-Bench: Can Large Language Models Engineer the Infrastructure That Powers Them?
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / LLM infrastructure engineering agents / benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: Benchmark grounded in real code repositories spans kernel completion through long-horizon end-to-end LLM-system optimization, directly measuring whether frontier LLMs can engineer the infrastructure stack. Important agentic AI-infra benchmark lineage, but not itself an efficiency technique.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Surface Imitation: Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment in Multimodal In-Context Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / adaptive reasoning / early exit
p1_watchlist.why: A lightweight alignment controller predicts response quality and decides whether another self-refinement step is needed, making iterative multimodal ICL conditional rather than unconditional. Relevant adaptive-inference lineage; no latency/token measurement in abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: CEDD-optimizer: Enabling Cost-Efficient Dataset Distillation on Geographically Distributed Edge Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / distributed dataset distillation / cost optimization
p1_watchlist.why: Optimizes dataset-distillation compression ratio and distillation steps across geographically distributed edge devices under heterogeneous energy and transfer prices. The abstract reports up to a 20.8 improvement over baseline under the same quality constraint, but the unit is not explicit in the primary abstract, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Storage-Scalable Progressive Semantic Communication via Knowledge-Base Reuse
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / semantic communication / storage efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Reuses a compact set of knowledge bases across progressive residual refinement stages, decoupling maintained-KB storage from transmission depth while preserving competitive semantic reconstruction. Useful edge/communication storage-efficiency evidence, but the abstract does not give a clean end-to-end AI serving latency or energy gain.

p1_watchlist.title: Orukeet: Multilingual ASR with Frozen Gabor Kernels
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient ASR / frozen structured filters
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces and freezes half of an adapted Parakeet encoder temporal filters with 12,288 fitted Gabor kernels while retaining the same inference operators; pooled FLEURS WER improves 11.01% to 9.85%. Retained as structured/frozen-model efficiency lineage, though the abstract does not establish end-to-end speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Belief-State Engine: Augmenting LLMs for Principled Planning Under Partial Observability
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / state abstraction / planning runtime
p1_watchlist.why: External Bayesian belief state replaces exposing the full raw action-observation history to an LLM and improves return, calibration and consistency on POMDP tasks. Retained as compact state-abstraction lineage for long-horizon agents; current abstract does not quantify token or latency savings.

p1_watchlist.title: AXON: A ROS 2 RMW with Shared-Memory/QUIC Transport and QKD/ML-KEM Key Establishment
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robotics middleware / edge-cloud transport
p1_watchlist.why: AXON replaces DDS-backed ROS 2 middleware with scope-aware transports: POSIX shared-memory rings on-host and QUIC remotely, plus explicit key-establishment modes. This is protected Physical-AI runtime/infra evidence; the current paper deliberately limits claims and does not yet provide comparative performance numbers.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboDrop: Curating VLA Post-Training Data via Local Gradient Compatibility
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / post-training data efficiency / data curation
p1_watchlist.why: RoboDrop scores robot demonstrations online during a one-epoch warm-up using local gradient compatibility against task-semantic and visually matched validation samples, then filters harmful episodes automatically. It targets the high cost and brittleness of VLA post-training data collection across controlled corruptions, simulation and real-robot datasets. This is protected Physical-AI data-efficiency work rather than an inference accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: MetroLLM-Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Transit Kiosk Runtimes
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / compact agent runtime / PEFT
p1_watchlist.why: MetroLLM-Bench shows a PEFT-trained Qwen 3.5 4B student with a 2.6 GB Q4_K_M footprint matching or exceeding much larger frontier models on deterministic kiosk-policy scoring, while larger 9B/27B students bring no Tier-1 gain. It is strong compact-agent deployment evidence, but the paper is primarily a benchmark and does not report end-to-end serving latency or cost.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Similarity: Foundation Models as an Efficient Backbone for Training-Free Composed Video Retrieval
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / adaptive inference depth / video retrieval
p1_watchlist.why: The framework uses reusable compact gallery embeddings first, then bounded reranking, candidate expansion, target-description generation and multimodal verification only for increasingly ambiguous cases. This is a useful adaptive-compute serving pattern for video retrieval, but the abstract emphasizes retrieval accuracy rather than measured latency or cost savings.

p1_watchlist.title: VLX-VR: An Agentic-Aware Video Reasoning Model
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / adaptive evidence acquisition / agent memory
p1_watchlist.why: VLX-VR uses a Think-Memory-Observation loop so a video reasoning model can adaptively acquire evidence, read or write memory, and decide when to terminate rather than relying on fixed-context single-pass processing. It is relevant to adaptive multimodal serving, but the abstract provides quality rather than latency or token-cost measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: ViBe: Visual Behavior Adaptation for Perceptive Humanoid Whole-Body Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / parameter-efficient robot adaptation / visual control
p1_watchlist.why: ViBe adapts pretrained humanoid motion trackers to perceptive control by extracting visual feedback and grafting it through low-rank adapters, enabling parameter-efficient post-training instead of rebuilding the controller. Protected Physical-AI adaptation lineage; abstract lacks a direct runtime or memory ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Numbat: Building and Verifying a Self-Contained Machine-Learning Stack
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / ML systems stack / deployment
p1_watchlist.why: Self-contained Zig ML stack with tensor/autodiff, mixed precision, multi-GPU training and a stable C ABI removes Python dependency chains and separate export/runtime toolchains. Full COCO training reaches near-reference accuracy with same-machine single-GPU step-time parity; retained as AI-infra stack/verifiability lineage rather than a speedup result.

p1_watchlist.title: When Does Low-Bit Quantization Preserve the Decisions of Vector Search?
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / vector search
p1_watchlist.why: decision-preserving low-bit quantization for vector retrieval

p1_watchlist.title: Can AI Agents Detect and Repair Artifact Drift in Network Experiments?
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent runtimes / benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: NetArtifactBench evaluates 23 agent configurations across three general-purpose AI-agent runtimes with deterministic scoring over 5,980 outputs. It is not an acceleration paper, but it is a useful systems benchmark for comparing runtime behavior and failure modes in multi-artifact workflows.

p1_watchlist.title: RealSimLoop: Online Real-to-Sim Adaptation via Differentiable Reduced-Order Simulation with Vision Feedback
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / differentiable simulation / online adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: RealSimLoop runs differentiable simulation in a reduced-order neural subspace and couples it with differentiable rendering for online vision-feedback parameter adaptation, reporting quasi-real-time operation and downstream force/stress estimation. This is directly relevant to efficient Physical-AI world-model/runtime loops, but the abstract lacks a clean speedup ratio or latency number.

p1_watchlist.title: UnitBoost: Managing Compound LLM Systems with a Merge Operator, Not a Model
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / compound LLM systems / non-generative orchestration
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces the generative meta-agent manager with an order-free merge operator and explicit residual-directed rounds, improving multiple compound-system configurations and removing a higher-level generative coordination step. It is highly relevant to agent serving efficiency, but the primary abstract does not provide a clean latency/token/cost reduction figure, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: GTA-2: A Multi-VLM Framework for Synthesizing Robot Manipulation Skills via Grounded Task Axes
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / multi-VLM skill synthesis / zero-shot manipulation / modular control
p1_watchlist.why: Factorizes manipulation into semantic subtasks, grounded task axes, controller parameters, and visual grounding using four specialized VLM agents, enabling zero-shot executable skill synthesis without robot demonstrations or task-specific fine-tuning. On 14 real-robot tasks it reaches 73.9% zero-shot success versus the strongest baseline by +31.4 points, rising to 90.7% with targeted refinement; this is high-value Physical-AI architecture evidence but not measured inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: Privacy-Preserving Split Learning for Federated LLM Fine-Tuning
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / federated LLM fine-tuning / split learning privacy
p1_watchlist.why: Partitions LLM fine-tuning across resource-constrained clients and a server, then adds learned obfuscate-and-recover protection against autoregressive activation leakage. The paper reports strong privacy with modest utility loss and system overhead; relevant to heterogeneous/federated LLM systems, but the primary source does not establish a strong acceleration win.

p1_watchlist.title: Procedural Memory Under Change: Reuse and Interference in Controlled Web Tasks
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / procedural memory / reuse under distribution shift
p1_watchlist.why: Controlled web-task experiments study when reusable procedural memory remains applicable after interface or task changes and when memory interferes. This is valuable negative systems evidence for agent skill reuse and memory portability, though no direct compute saving is claimed.

p1_watchlist.title: SymbolicLight V2: Hybrid Neuromorphic Architecture and Sparse Execution for Low-Energy Language Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI / sparse inference / FPGA
p1_watchlist.why: Hybrid neuromorphic language architecture implemented on Alveo U50C and ARM. Same-checkpoint FPGA variants raise decode throughput from 474.6 to 643.2 tok/s and cut gross card energy/token 27.6%; however the deployed checkpoint trails a same-budget dense control in quality, so the paper does not establish equal-quality efficiency and remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: CT-SAFR: Safe and Interpretable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Robots: A Multi-Layered Verification Framework for Trustworthy AI-Driven Robotic Decision Making
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / runtime verification / robot reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: CT-SAFR adds a multi-layer robot-reasoning verifier with 94.2% hallucination detection and sub-500 ms latency in a warehouse-robot case study. This is protected Physical-AI runtime-verification evidence, although the contribution is safety rather than acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: Introducing Consort: A Spec-First Agent Framework for Enforced, Test-Driven Development on Live Database Branches
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / coding-agent infrastructure / deterministic orchestration
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a deterministic orchestrator, immutable tests, human-approved gates and live database branches so non-deterministic coding agents cannot bypass engineering controls. Valuable production-agent harness lineage; no measured runtime/token reduction yet.

p1_watchlist.title: PRAGMA: Evaluating Personalized Guidance with Memory Alignment in Lifelong Conversations
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / retrieval benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: PRAGMA targets the computational and reliability problems of full conversational histories and evaluates retrieval, memory and long-context systems for personalized guidance. It is a useful long-term-memory systems benchmark, but the abstract does not quantify end-to-end token or latency savings.

p1_watchlist.title: A Risk-Sensitive and Uncertainty-Aware Decision-Making and Control Framework for Safe and Robust Autonomous Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / autonomous driving / adaptive safety runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Uses policy uncertainty to adapt control-barrier strictness and a residual predictor for model mismatch, balancing safety and efficiency while satisfying real-time requirements. Protected Physical-AI runtime lineage rather than a pure acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: JEPA Policy: Diffusion-Free Imitation Learning via Paired Action and Future Representation Prediction
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / diffusion-free action policy / low-latency visuomotor imitation
p1_watchlist.why: Uses paired action and future-representation prediction instead of iterative diffusion sampling. Across nine simulated tasks it improves over MIP and outperforms Diffusion Policy under evaluated settings while adding only 0.29 ms to MIP model latency; a five-task 630-episode real-robot study preserves the ranking. Strong protected Physical-AI signal, but the primary abstract does not quantify speedup versus Diffusion Policy, so retained as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Benchmarking Agentic HLS Design Tasks With HLS-Eval
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / hardware design automation / agent cost profiling
p1_watchlist.why: Extends HLS-Eval with an agentic flow that edits code, compiles for self-verification, iterates during inference, and logs cost, token usage, and iteration count. Highly relevant to AI-for-hardware workflow efficiency and tool-use evaluation, but it is primarily a benchmark rather than a demonstrated acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: HLSFactory-Agent: Large-Scale Agentic HLS Dataset Construction from Academic and Open-Source Projects
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / hardware design agents / HLS infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: HLSFactory-Agent runs an open-source coding-agent stack in Docker to extract, build and evaluate standalone HLS designs from larger repositories and pairs this with architecture/EDA/FPGA paper indexing. Useful agentic compiler/hardware infrastructure lineage, though current evidence is dataset-construction automation rather than model inference efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: Agentic AI-enabled Semantic Commissioning of a Cognitive Digital Twin for Reconfigurable Manufacturing
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / industrial agents / runtime orchestration
p1_watchlist.why: A LangGraph multi-agent workflow combines RAG and MCP-based telemetry binding for a robotic machining cell and reports reducing commissioning from several weeks to about two hours. It is strong workflow-efficiency evidence for industrial Physical AI, but the gain is deployment-process automation rather than model inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: Actuator Dynamics Curricula for Narrow-Viability Tasks in Legged Robot Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot policy training / curriculum efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI training lineage: actuator-dynamics curriculum expands the viable exploration region so a quadruped handstand task that fails under fixed identified stiffness becomes trainable and transfers to Boston Dynamics Spot hardware. It improves training feasibility rather than inference speed.

p1_watchlist.title: Learning Global Camera Poses from Noisy View-Graphs for Structure from Motion
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 3D perception / scalable pose estimation
p1_watchlist.why: Permutation-equivariant view-graph aggregation estimates globally consistent camera poses, scales beyond one thousand images and is reported much faster than state-of-the-art classical pipelines. Relevant scalable 3D perception lineage; abstract omits a wall-clock ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Efficient Fairness Auditing Across Guidance Scales in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Causal Abstraction
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / amortized evaluation / text-to-image
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces repeated exhaustive generation across classifier-free-guidance settings with a causal abstraction and probabilistic-transformer predictor over abstract denoising states. The paper explicitly evaluates computational efficiency, making it relevant as amortized diffusion-evaluation lineage, but the abstract reports no numerical speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / edge agents / on-device SLM / function calling
p1_watchlist.why: Benchmarks Functional Tokens versus Schema-in-Prompt for 270M-1.7B on-device vehicle agents across 9,822 examples and 79 Android Automotive functions, explicitly exposing the compact-inference versus unseen-function-generalization tradeoff. Important protected edge-Physical-AI evidence, but no exact latency or memory numbers are reported in the abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: OmniEye: Efficient Multimodal Forensic Video Intelligence for Law-Enforcement Body-Worn Cameras
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge deployment / quantization
p1_watchlist.why: OmniEye processes 30-second audiovisual windows with a multimodal foundation model, stores structured outputs in SQLite/BM25, and re-perceives only retrieved candidate windows for grounded questioning. The complete system is reported to run on a single 16 GB GPU using a 4-bit quantization-aware-trained model, giving useful deployment evidence for retrieval-gated multimodal serving, but without a direct speedup baseline.

p1_watchlist.title: Do Agents Know When They Succeed? Calibrating Agent Confidence from Internal Representations
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / runtime reliability / confidence monitoring
p1_watchlist.why: Uses residual-stream trajectory dynamics and action-representation probes to predict eventual agent success across Bash, SQL, and Python tasks and three model families. It reports a zero-overhead reliability monitor requiring neither prompt changes nor multi-sample rollouts; highly relevant to low-cost agent runtime control, but the abstract does not quantify end-to-end serving savings.

p1_watchlist.title: Efficient Leakage-Free Neural Architecture Search under Leave-One-Subject-Out Evaluation
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / neural architecture search / model compression
p1_watchlist.why: Block-based leakage-free NAS avoids fully nested O(N^2) search and reduces model parameters by up to 99.2% on BioVid while slightly improving mean accuracy. Good resource-efficiency evidence, but currently narrow in task/domain and lacks standardized GPU-hour reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: QPS-ToR: A Parallel Iterative Switching Algorithm for Reconfigurable Optical Datacenter Switching
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / datacenter networking / optical switching / low-complexity scheduling
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces single-iteration iSLIP in a reconfigurable optical datacenter fabric with sliding-window QPS and, in 128-ToR flow simulations, reports up to 36% higher throughput and 82% lower flow completion time versus NegotiaToR. The system result is strong, but the current paper is workload-agnostic rather than AI-specific, so it is retained as high-value AI-infrastructure networking evidence instead of canonical strong.

p1_watchlist.title: VANTAGE-Bench: Evaluating the Infrastructure AI Gap in Vision-Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / fixed-camera infrastructure VLM benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: Benchmarks 17 VLMs across logistics, transportation and smart-space infrastructure video, including long-horizon tracking and spatio-temporal tasks. Exposes a distinct Physical-AI deployment gap and releases evaluation harness/leaderboard; benchmark rather than acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Encrypt What Matters: When Selective Homomorphic Inference Is Efficient
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / privacy-preserving inference / selective FHE
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that encrypting only sensitive ROIs can preserve exact outputs while locality-preserving architectures obtain order-of-magnitude homomorphic-evaluation speedups, whereas early global mixing removes the benefit. This is valuable architectural efficiency evidence, but the abstract presents conditional rather than a single deployment-wide benchmark, so it is retained as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / AI-RAN / low-latency inference
p1_watchlist.why: NOSTRAdAMUS deploys a predictive link-adaptation dApp with 5.5 microsecond inference latency and reports up to 71.5% goodput improvement and 71.8% retransmission reduction on real and hardware-in-the-loop 5G setups. It is strong edge-runtime evidence, though the workload is network control rather than AI-model serving itself.

p1_watchlist.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / procedural memory / long-horizon tool use
p1_watchlist.why: Externalizes procedural knowledge into a self-evolving graph and localizes the active procedure node before each action, addressing repeated or out-of-order tool calls in long trajectories. Strong runtime-structure relevance, but the abstract does not provide a clean serving-cost or latency gain, so it remains watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: Proxy Policy Steering
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / inference-time adaptation / flow policy steering
p1_watchlist.why: Inference-time adaptation trains lightweight reference and task proxy policies whose velocity-space residual steers a frozen generalist sampler at every denoising step. Across 8 real and 4 simulation manipulation tasks it improves pi-0.5 by 53% absolute success on average while retaining broad base capabilities; strong Physical-AI relevance, but no measured serving latency/compute reduction in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / harness optimization / small-model deployment
p1_watchlist.why: Studies co-evolution of agent harnesses and lightweight model adaptation across seven enterprise tasks. Evolved harnesses let weaker models approach stronger-model behavior at lower deployment cost, while naive expert-trajectory imitation can regress 4-30 points. Strong evidence that runtime scaffolding and model adaptation must be co-designed, but the abstract does not provide a clean latency/token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: Mask Forcing: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion Distillation via Dual-Noise Masking Rollout
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / diffusion distillation / autoregressive video generation
p1_watchlist.why: Improves causal autoregressive video diffusion students distilled from bidirectional teachers using dual-noise spatial-temporal masking during self-rollout. Directly relevant to real-time video diffusion distillation; current abstract emphasizes efficient quality gains but gives no clean latency/speedup number.

p1_watchlist.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / dexterous manipulation / tactile fusion / world modeling
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI candidate. DeCAL combines specialized MoT experts, adaptive visuo-tactile fusion, and latent co-imagination for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, reaching 71% average success and 83.4% progress success. The current primary abstract does not report serving latency, throughput, memory, or a comparative runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent memory / context management
p1_watchlist.why: Task-conditioned memory clearance uses LOO screening plus sampled cooperative Shapley attribution to suppress harmful memories without modifying the persistent store. Across ten long-dialogue memory pools it reaches 85.9% target recall and 82.3% task recovery, +25.5 points over LOO, but no direct token/latency reduction is reported, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Ozaki 2.5: Engineering the Deconstruction Path of fp64-Emulated Dense Matrix Multiplication on FP8 Tensor Cores
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / FP8 tensor cores / mixed precision / GEMM / architecture co-design
p1_watchlist.why: High-value mixed-precision architecture/kernel work on FP64-emulated GEMM over FP8 tensor cores, including residue conversion, pipelining and a proposed stream-side conversion mechanism. The paper explicitly states that every performance result is a model projection pending measurement, so projected 235-473 TFLOPS and 1.6-1.9x gains are not promoted as measured systems evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: It's Not RoPE that Creates Sinks: The Role of Self-Concentration and Value-Non-Mixing in Attention
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / attention / massive activations / low-bit robustness
p1_watchlist.why: Mechanistic analysis directly relevant to low-bit quantization: it attributes attention sinks and massive activations to causal-mask-induced self-concentration and value non-mixing rather than RoPE. It may inform future quantization strategies, but it proposes no quantizer and reports no measured inference efficiency benefit, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Rethinking Learned Occupancy in Autonomous Active Mapping with Observation-Gated Filtering
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / active mapping
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that more accurate learned occupancy can still hurt closed-loop mapping, then adds an observation-gated planner-facing filter without retraining. This is protected Physical-AI evidence about online world-model correction, not direct inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: PlayTrain: An Efficient Reinforcement Learning Framework for LLM-Generated Adaptable JavaScript Games
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / RL infrastructure / simulation throughput
p1_watchlist.why: Combines LLM-generated JavaScript environments with a high-throughput RL pipeline and reports over 1M agent decisions per second on a single GPU node. This is strong infrastructure evidence for cheap scalable agent-environment generation and training, but it is not directly an LLM serving or inference acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / model editing / training-free adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Maps activation steering vectors to rank-one weight-space edits using forward-pass statistics only, avoiding fine-tuning to discover task vectors while supporting add/subtract/composition operations. Strong adaptation-efficiency idea, but the abstract does not quantify deployment latency or memory savings.

p1_watchlist.title: Omni Interaction Agent Technical Report
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / efficient reasoning/agent systems / streaming full-duplex runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Gander is directly relevant to realtime multimodal agent infrastructure: a Cerebellum-Brain split, streaming Thinker-Talker, chunk-level ordered token stream, tool calling and an agent orchestration runtime support continuous full-duplex video/speech/text interaction and interruption. The primary report does not give hard end-to-end latency/throughput numbers for the orchestration design, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: GraphFAS: A Distributed System for Automated Graph Feature Generation and Selection in Industrial Transaction Networks
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / industrial graph systems / feature pipeline / production deployment
p1_watchlist.why: Production distributed graph-feature system deployed at Alipay, with explicit graph feature generation and distributed Boruta-style selection and reported order-of-magnitude engineering-efficiency improvement. This is useful production infrastructure evidence, but the abstract lacks a concrete throughput/latency/speedup baseline, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: SkillAdam: Stable and Efficient Skill Evolution for Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / skill optimization / agent memory / cost reduction
p1_watchlist.why: Relevant efficient-agent work: optimization memory stabilizes discrete skill updates and a volatility-driven edit budget adapts revision scope; across seven benchmarks it reports stronger skills with substantially fewer optimization iterations and lower cost than prior methods. Because the primary abstract gives no concrete wall-clock/token/cost reduction numbers, it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: OTTER - Two Transistor - One RRAM Architecture for Reliable In-Memory-Computing in 28 nm CMOS Technology
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compute-in-memory / RRAM accelerator
p1_watchlist.why: 28 nm CMOS plus TaOx RRAM 2T1R platform demonstrates six-level analog conductance and hardware CIM MACs on a 15x15 crossbar. Relevant accelerator/CIM lineage; abstract emphasizes reliability and circuit operation rather than end-to-end AI speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: FRAME: Factored Retrieval via Attribute Readouts for Object-Centric Scene Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / scene memory / retrieval
p1_watchlist.why: FRAME factors language queries into attribute weights over a fixed object-centric scene memory, targeting persistent robot-memory retrieval without rerunning perception. Protected Physical-AI memory lineage, but the abstract focuses on retrieval quality rather than measured compute savings.

p1_watchlist.title: DiffLUT-Net: Differentiable Training of FPGA LUT Networks with Learnable Connectivity
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI / FPGA / hardware-native networks
p1_watchlist.why: FPGA-native networks jointly learn six-input LUT truth tables and sparse connectivity, then export directly to synthesizable Verilog and prune unused logic. It reports favorable accuracy-resource tradeoffs across five benchmarks and releases code, but the abstract provides no exact latency/energy/throughput advantage, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Exploring the Genesis Platform Capabilities to Accelerate Scientific Discovery in OPAL
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / cross-facility orchestration / managed AI services
p1_watchlist.why: DOE Genesis provides reusable managed execution, model distribution, governed LLM access, shared data and provenance across facilities; in a 40-day campaign it replaced roughly twelve hours of manual analysis with interactive queries returning in seconds to minutes.

p1_watchlist.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / episodic memory / production consistency
p1_watchlist.why: Converts unstable agent trajectory steps into episodic guidelines. On AppWorld with ReAct/GPT-4.1, all-five-runs success improves by +16 points same-task and +13 points similar-task. High-value agent-runtime reliability work, but not direct inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: ArmPoser: Real-Time, Calibration-Free Arm Pose Estimation from Smartwatch IMU
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge sensing / real-time pose estimation
p1_watchlist.why: Physical-AI/edge protected item: ArmPoser eliminates coordinate transforms, explicit alignment, and user bone-offset calibration by learning directly in device-native smartwatch coordinates, while matching or exceeding calibrated baselines in real-time deployment studies. Efficiency is workflow/deployment simplification rather than a quantified accelerator result.

p1_watchlist.title: Hi-FLoop: Hierarchical State-Feedback Loops for Multi-Timescale World Modeling
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / world models / multi-timescale closed-loop generation
p1_watchlist.why: Hierarchical branch-consistent traffic world model separates 8-s Goal, 2-s Preview, 1-s Control, and 0.5-s feedback commits, with sparse future interaction graphs and generated-state recovery. It directly matches multi-timescale Physical-AI system structure, but currently reports predictive quality rather than serving/runtime savings, so it remains protected watch.

p1_watchlist.title: A Note on Scaling in Randomly Rotated Quantization and Its Connection to the CDEF +1 Pythagorean Relation
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization
p1_watchlist.why: finite-dimensional theory for randomized-rotation quantization; useful lineage for rotation-based low-bit quantization

p1_watchlist.title: No Free Checker: A Survey of Verifiers for Robot Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / policy verification / runtime monitors
p1_watchlist.why: This survey organizes roughly 150 robot-policy verifiers around availability (cost, latency, density) and credibility, directly exposing the runtime cost-versus-trust tradeoff for VLA policy checking. It is a protected Physical-AI reference rather than an acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Tools-CC-Bench: a Benchmark Suite for Collective Communication with Compression in HPC and AI Workloads
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / collective communication / compression / systems benchmarking
p1_watchlist.why: 7d replay recovered an application-oriented benchmark for compression-enabled collectives across realistic HPC and LLM workloads. CC-Bench profiles per-phase latency, hardware utilization, fidelity and computation interference across CPU/GPU clusters and multiple communication libraries. It is highly relevant infrastructure for communication-compression evaluation, but the abstract primarily contributes methodology and characterization rather than a new universally faster runtime, so it is retained as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Hyperparameter Scaling Laws Across MoE Sparsity
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / sparse training / scaling laws
p1_watchlist.why: The work runs 1,800 pre-training experiments spanning six activated-parameter scales, about 20T tokens and 200k H800-equivalent GPU-hours, deriving scaling laws that explicitly include activation ratio and validating on a 12B ultra-sparse MoE with 1/64 experts active. It is important MoE efficiency methodology but does not introduce a measured systems/runtime speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: BIFTA: Brain-Inspired Few-Shot Tactile Adaptation for Unknown Sensors
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / tactile sensing / few-shot adaptation / heterogeneous sensors
p1_watchlist.why: Adapts a frozen tactile encoder to previously unseen sensor hardware using a small labeled support set, dual-view statistical memory, spectral graphs, and uncertainty-gated propagation. With 10% labeled target data on SITR, mean Sparsh accuracy rises from 6.86% to 87.09%, but this is data-efficient adaptation rather than measured inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: MoEMB: Scaling Universal Multimodal Embeddings with Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Models
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / MoE systems / retrieval embeddings
p1_watchlist.why: MoEMB scales universal multimodal embeddings along the expert axis and studies adaptive computation. With only 3B active parameters it surpasses reasoning-token embedding methods using over 4x active parameters, but the current abstract emphasizes active compute and quality rather than measured serving latency or throughput, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: CoordFormer: Give Me Any Coordinates and I Will Give You Labels
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / high-resolution inference / edge-cloud vision
p1_watchlist.why: Coordinate decoding with localized cross-attention combines downsampled global ViT tokens and high-resolution local patches, supporting semantic-edge-focused inference that reduces memory, latency and compute on very-high-resolution segmentation. SOTA accuracy is reported, but the abstract omits exact speedup/memory numbers, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: TriCCOT: Tri-part Convolutional Conformal Transformer for Onboard Space Object Detection
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / FPGA / efficient attention
p1_watchlist.why: TriCCOT replaces FPGA-unfriendly Transformer operations with convolutional projections, global channel statistics and hardware-friendly gating, and reports full unified CNN-Transformer deployment on a Xilinx Versal VCK190 without DPU modification. This is strong deployability evidence, but the primary abstract does not give measured latency, throughput, memory or energy gains, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Difficulty-Adaptive Tree-Structured Policy Optimization for Expanding Reasoning Coverage in RLVR
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / RLVR / adaptive rollouts
p1_watchlist.why: Difficulty-adaptive tree rollouts and entropy-guided branching allocate training exploration according to problem difficulty and improve pass@k/test-time scaling. Direct adaptive-rollout efficiency mechanism, but abstract emphasizes reasoning coverage rather than measured training-cost reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: CLAMP: Constrained Decoding for Vision-Language Embodied Planning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embodied planning / constrained decoding
p1_watchlist.why: Uses scene evidence and a symbolic action model to hard-mask infeasible next tokens and HMM lookahead to reweight feasible actions for a frozen VLM planner. Protected Physical-AI decoding/runtime lineage with no model retraining.

p1_watchlist.title: BIO-MEMART: Biometric-Aware KV Cache Memory for Multi-User LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning/agent systems / shared memory
p1_watchlist.why: Bio-MemArt adds biometric authorization to reusable KV-memory blocks while preserving MemArt latent retrieval and direct cache reuse. Its efficiency study reduces average prefill tokens from 18,781.96 full-context to 28.57, but the main novelty is access control rather than serving acceleration, so retain as a high-value KV/agent watch.

p1_watchlist.title: CreaMem: A Scene-Aware Memory Architecture for Personalized Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / retrieval organization
p1_watchlist.why: Partitions long-term agent memory by life scene and dual-codes memories from episodic and trait perspectives, directly targeting retrieval-space inflation and cross-scene interference. It is useful lineage for efficient agent memory organization, but the primary abstract does not establish a clean latency/token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: PGMT: Perceptive General Motion Tracking for Humanoid Robots
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / humanoid runtime / selective terrain perception
p1_watchlist.why: Physical-AI protected item: PGMT uses motion-conditioned terrain glimpses to selectively encode terrain regions relevant to the current motion and demonstrates zero-shot Unitree G1 deployment over complex real terrain. Selective perception is runtime-relevant, though the paper reports robustness rather than compute savings.

p1_watchlist.title: Temporal State Transport in Video Generation: Diagnosing and Correcting Spectral Imbalance
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / training-free video control
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a training-free regulator that selectively corrects only pathological temporal-attention states while largely preserving balanced states, improving temporal consistency without finetuning. Useful adaptive-compute/control lineage, though runtime overhead is not quantified.

p1_watchlist.title: AURORA: Active Uncertainty-Driven Re-Orientation for In-Hand Reconstruction
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / active perception / adaptive 3D reconstruction
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime: uncertainty-novelty next-best-view planning actively acquires only informative observations and uses lightweight geometric fusion. The project reports a reference reconstruction latency of 71.82 s versus 417.13 s for Neural Feels (about 5.8x lower), while explicitly noting hardware/task differences.

p1_watchlist.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / embodied agents / long-term memory / safety
p1_watchlist.why: CoRL 2026 SafeMem maintains a long-term semantic graph under partial observability and uses an LLM risk predictor plus conservatism-modulated replanning. It substantially improves safe success on IS-Bench and a real robot platform, making it a protected Physical-AI memory/safety node, but it reports no serving or compute-efficiency metric.

p1_watchlist.title: AirAnchor: Bridging Local and Global Spatial Information for Zero-Shot Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / local-global memory / aerial VLN
p1_watchlist.why: AirAnchor bridges online local representations and offline global memories using spatial anchors for zero-shot aerial VLN. It is protected Physical-AI memory/orchestration lineage, but the abstract focuses on navigation quality rather than measured inference efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: AI-Native Orchestration in the 6G Continuum: Evolving Operator Platforms with Agentic AI
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems
p1_watchlist.why: agentic cloud-edge-IoT orchestration with persistent service context, closed-loop resource optimization and cross-domain SLA control

p1_watchlist.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming speech / modular adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: AV-STE is a streaming audio-visual token-restoration front-end that keeps the downstream Moshi speech LLM frozen, avoiding costly multimodal retraining while improving coherence under noise. Useful modular serving lineage, but the abstract gives no end-to-end latency or throughput comparison.

p1_watchlist.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / RL post-training / serving-training integration
p1_watchlist.why: Full-stack post-training system built around SGLang rollouts, Megatron/FSDP training and multiple weight-sync transports, with asynchronous agentic RL demonstrated on GLM-5.2 744B-A40B over 64 GB300 GPUs. Important open AI-infra evidence, though the abstract lacks a clean baseline speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboCousin: Build Your Own Simulation Playground for Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / synthetic data systems / bimanual manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI data-system work that converts user observations into simulation-ready assets, scenes, grasp-contact annotations and expert trajectories. RoboCousin-OBD contains over 3,000 object instances and 50 environments, and the pipeline generates over one million trajectories across 50 tasks with sim-to-real validation. It improves data scalability rather than inference latency, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / distillation / RL post-training
p1_watchlist.why: RouteOPD turns sampled on-policy distillation into explicit teacher-guided probability transport, directing updates only from student-excess sources to teacher-deficit destinations and improving reasoning benchmarks with lower background leakage.

p1_watchlist.title: EdMCGS: Event-Driven Markov Chain Gaussian Splatting for Extreme-Low-Frame-Rate Dynamic Scene Reconstruction
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 3DGS / real-time dynamic reconstruction
p1_watchlist.why: Event-driven control points propagate motion between sparse RGB frames and render dynamic scenes in real time using far fewer Gaussians than the strongest event-based baseline. Direct efficient 3D scene-representation lineage; abstract lacks a comparable wall-clock number.

p1_watchlist.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / LLM inference / measurement
p1_watchlist.why: This controlled study measures accuracy, footprint, prefill latency, per-token latency and execution energy across Jetson AGX Orin and near-edge CPU/GPU nodes, including quantized open models and cloud GPT-4o as a reference. It provides useful placement and Pareto evidence but introduces no new serving mechanism, so retain as a high-value measurement watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Distribution-Consistent Inference for Dynamic Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / dynamic routing / sparse inference
p1_watchlist.why: Findings EMNLP 2026 identifies representation-scale shift when inference-time top-k is reduced and proposes lightweight layer-wise distribution alignment using calibration statistics. It recovers much of the lost quality while preserving dynamic sparse-routing efficiency with negligible overhead, but the primary abstract gives no concrete latency/FLOP/throughput reduction, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Scaling Post-Training Ternarisation to Qwen3-8B Capability Retention, Reproduction, Lossless Packing, and Packed Execution
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / ultra-low-bit LLM / packed execution / deployment characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Provides an end-to-end Qwen3-8B ternarisation and deployment characterization including lossless packing and direct packed execution at 15.52 tokens/s in 7.35 GiB. It is valuable negative/engineering evidence because the preliminary packed GEMV is still slower than FP16 cuBLAS, so it is retained as watch rather than promoted as an acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: SAM3-O2D2: Zero-Shot Object Out-of-Distribution Detection by Object Class Prompting of the SAM3-Image Model
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / efficient vision inference / OOD detection
p1_watchlist.why: The method explicitly replaces a prior zero-shot OOD pipeline whose inference requires computationally costly diffusion with a SAM3-image prompting route. This is relevant foundation-model inference-efficiency lineage, but the abstract does not provide a clean wall-clock speedup or energy ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Seeing is Not Believing: Breaking the Physical-to-Digital Trust Boundary in Robotics
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI: ROS 2 telemetry/control interception is demonstrated on a physical Franka arm with ~3 ms jitter; relevant embodied-runtime infrastructure/security evidence, not an acceleration contribution.

p1_watchlist.title: What Eviction Destroys: A Restore-Counterfactual Audit of Forgetting in Agent Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory eviction / evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a per-question restore counterfactual that separates irreversible eviction loss from recoverable retrieval failure under token budgets. It is a useful diagnostic for agent-memory compression policies, though it is an audit methodology rather than an optimizer.
