p1_watchlist.title: Revoked but Still Authoritative: An Empirical Study of Revocation Enforcement in Agent-Memory Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Agent-memory revocation study identifies a retrieval-time failure across persistent-memory systems and adds a backend-agnostic guard; useful agent memory/runtime systems lineage, but compute efficiency is secondary.

p1_watchlist.title: CALIPER: Clean Scenes Cannot Rank Physical Inference in Pretrained Visual Representations
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / representation evaluation / world models
p1_watchlist.why: CALIPER shows clean fixed-camera probes can falsely make random and pretrained encoders look equally physical, while randomized scenes expose a large spread in actionable prediction. Useful protected Physical-AI evaluation debt for choosing perception backbones.

p1_watchlist.title: Agentic ML Exploration (A-MLE) for Ads Ranking
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / ML infrastructure / autonomous experimentation / industrial ranking
p1_watchlist.why: Industrial autonomous ML-exploration system deployed across a portfolio of large-scale ads-ranking models, coordinating hypothesis generation, experiment execution, analysis and shared knowledge with sandboxed tools and human checkpoints. It directly targets the human-throughput bottleneck of ML iteration, but the primary abstract does not expose a clean quantitative latency, compute, or cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: SE-GoS: Self-Evolving Graph-of-Skills for Skill Library at Scale
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / scalable skill retrieval / token efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free evolution of a Graph-of-Skills from execution traces improves retrieval quality while reducing context load. On SkillsBench, a representative round raises reward from 52.4% to 59.4% while reducing input tokens by about one-third relative to full skill loading; directly relevant to scalable agent skill/memory infrastructure.

p1_watchlist.title: 3DWay: Generalizing Robot Manipulation via 3D Consistent Waypoints
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving
p1_watchlist.why: 3D-consistent waypoint interface for robot manipulation

p1_watchlist.title: Drive by Hindsight and Foresight: Tool-Grounded Synergistic Reasoning over Hierarchical Memory for Autonomous Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / autonomous driving / hierarchical memory / proactive tool invocation
p1_watchlist.why: Couples scene-level short-term memory, evolving long-term experience memory and adaptive tool invocation in a closed reasoning loop. Its 7B model reaches 79.09% MCQ on DriveLMM-o1, with short-term memory improving STSBench by 24.2 points and frozen-parameter long-term memory adding 3.57 MCQ points. It is valuable Physical-AI memory/tool-use evidence, but the reported contribution is capability rather than inference efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: Monkey See, Can Monkey Do? A Benchmark for Evaluating Robot Skill Learning by Observation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot learning / data scaling benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: RoboReel provides a unified benchmark for learning robot policies from human videos across ten manipulation tasks and seven-plus algorithms including VLA variants. It directly addresses robotics data scaling and long-horizon robustness, but is a benchmark rather than an inference accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: Qiushi Engine on AstaBench E2E-Bench-Hard
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / autonomous research agents / cost evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: Reports an end-to-end autonomous research-agent evaluation with explicit average benchmark cost of USD 15.209 per task and full execution traces across 40 hard tasks. Useful cost-aware agent-systems evidence, though it is primarily an engine evaluation rather than a new efficiency mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: Do Dynamic Routers Need Memory? HeRo: History-Aware Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / dynamic layer routing / efficient LLM inference / router memory
p1_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a relevant dynamic-routing paper absent from authority. HeRo conditions token-wise FFN routing on an explicit history state built with linear attention; on Llama 3.1-8B it reports 100.24% dense-model aggregate performance while bypassing 26.87% of parameters, and 97.01% performance while bypassing 38.82%. Retained as high-value watch because the abstract does not report measured wall-clock latency or throughput gains.

p1_watchlist.title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / routing harness / post-training infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a heterogeneous model pool plus intelligent routing to record capability demand, chosen service tier and tool/harness traces, then converts them into validated curricula and routing-guided on-policy distillation. Relevant agent-infra feedback-loop lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Less Is Personal: Learning Minimal Sufficient User Profiles for Personalized Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / context compression / personalization
p1_watchlist.why: ENOUGH learns when to STOP adding retrieved user history, jointly optimizing utility, specificity and token cost, then invokes the frozen generator once. Across six personalization tasks it preserves utility while reducing unnecessary context, but the abstract does not state a single comparable token-reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Dual-Layer Semantic-Spatial Belief Mapping for Aerial Object Goal Navigation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / persistent spatial memory / VLM navigation
p1_watchlist.why: AeroBelief converts noisy frame-level VLM outputs into persistent semantic-spatial belief maps with separate intuition and evidence layers for aerial ObjectNav. Protected Physical-AI memory/runtime lineage; efficiency is architectural rather than measured as latency or FLOPs.

p1_watchlist.title: WorldAgen: Unified State-Action Prediction with Test-Time World Model Training
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / test-time adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work unifying world-state prediction and action prediction with lightweight test-time training to adapt world dynamics in unseen environments. It improves CALVIN/LIBERO performance after a small number of test-time samples, but the primary abstract gives no measured test-time overhead, latency or throughput, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: OmniNav: Robust Long-Horizon Target Navigation in Dynamic Environments
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / long-horizon navigation / persistent scene memory / closed-loop recovery
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains an updatable 3D object scene memory, revises target beliefs under partial observability, and propagates execution feedback through hierarchical closed-loop recovery. It improves real-world pick-and-place success from 53.3% to 71.7% over an adapted open-loop baseline. This is strong protected evidence for persistent embodied memory and closed-loop execution, but it does not claim inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: KBBQ: A Predictive Noise Law and the Limits of Spectrum Flattening in FP4 Quantization
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / FP4 / W4A4 / transform-based quantization
p1_watchlist.why: High-value FP4 quantization work with a closed-form second-order noise law and Kappa-Braked Blockwise Quantization. Across four base models and two FP4 formats, KBBQ improves W4A4 quality over prior state of the art without additional deployment-time computation. The primary abstract does not report measured latency/throughput or memory speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Sparse Data Augmentation for Optimization with Provable Guarantees
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient training / data augmentation / optimization
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that a fixed sparse set of transformations can approximate full group augmentation with O((log|G|+log(1/delta))/epsilon^2) transformation queries versus O(1/epsilon^4) for group-SGD, giving a principled training-efficiency route for symmetry-heavy ML.

p1_watchlist.title: Jacap: Robust KV Cache Eviction via Jacobian-Based Nonlinear Information Capacity Preservation
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / eviction / information geometry / cache compression
p1_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a theoretically grounded KV-cache eviction method absent from authority. Jacap derives a Jacobian information-capacity objective for nonlinear softmax attention and uses softmax-aware importance plus statistical leverage scores for cache subset selection, with strongest gains reported in high-compression regimes. Retained as high-value watch because the current evidence is quality-under-compression rather than measured serving latency/throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Observe Before You Alert: Adaptive Driver Alerting with Vision-Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive perception / driver alerting
p1_watchlist.why: VLAlert introduces SILENT/OBSERVE/ALERT actions so a VLM can delay uncertain warnings and adapt the next observation window. It is relevant to adaptive Physical-AI perception and runtime control, but reports decision quality rather than inference speed or compute reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: DISEIL: Demonstration Distillation for Sample-Efficient Imitation Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / imitation learning / data efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Clusters recurring robot-policy failure modes and asks for targeted demonstrations starting at the first unreliable step. Across five simulated tasks and both state/image observations it achieves the highest mean held-out success in all ten settings, with the largest margin at the smallest demonstration budget. Important Physical-AI data-efficiency evidence, though not inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: Router Prior Bias: Preserving Base Routing Structure in MoE Post-Training
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / router post-training / expert co-activation
p1_watchlist.why: Shows downstream MoE post-training benefits from softly preserving the pretrained router prior rather than re-imposing uniform load balancing. Important expert-routing lineage on Moonlight-16B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, but no measured serving throughput/latency gain in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: Nyström Attention Matches Full Attention for Cross-Sectional Stock Prediction
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / low-rank attention / linear-complexity approximation
p1_watchlist.why: This controlled attention decomposition finds the learned cross-sectional attention deviation to be low-rank and shows Nystrom attention with 32 landmarks matches full O(N^2) attention at O(mN) cost, with statistical equivalence at N=300 and N=800. It is useful evidence for low-rank rather than sparse attention structure, but the primary abstract does not report measured latency, throughput, memory or energy gains, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / dense vision / single-step inference
p1_watchlist.why: Marigold V2 converts pretrained multi-step flow-matching image models into single-step dense-regression inference, with quantization where needed, while improving KITTI/ETH3D AbsRel by 16-26% over the previous best. The step-count reduction is strategically relevant to diffusion/flow acceleration, but the current abstract does not report measured end-to-end latency or throughput, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Inference-Time Nash Alignment
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / inference-time adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces parameter-updating preference fine-tuning with inference-time Best-of-Nash and Nash Mirror Descent under general preferences. It is relevant as a no-fine-tuning alignment path, but the abstract provides no direct end-to-end compute or latency comparison.

p1_watchlist.title: ResidualAuth: What Authorization State Must Language Agents Preserve under Revocable Delegation?
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent memory / state compression
p1_watchlist.why: Shows a concrete lower-bound-style failure of overly compressed agent memory: a fixed 256-token summary solves at most 2/16 paired authorization cases, while exact ledger serializations fit held-out states at 768-1024 tokens and support correct decisions. Valuable negative evidence for how far agent runtime state can be compressed.

p1_watchlist.title: Eliciting Self-Verification in Multimodal Reasoning Agents with Reinforcement Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal tool use / self-verification
p1_watchlist.why: SVRL trains multimodal agents to verify and filter retrieved evidence internally, adds a search-aware penalty against unnecessary tool calls, and reports consistent gains in tool efficiency while narrowing the gap between compact open models and much larger proprietary systems with substantially lower training and inference cost. The primary abstract does not provide a clean end-to-end latency or cost ratio, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: TaskGuard: Task-Conditioned Restoration Utility for Risk-Aware Object Detection
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive perception / conditional preprocessing
p1_watchlist.why: TaskGuard is a post-hoc controller for frozen restoration+detection pipelines that predicts whether a restoration intervention should be used. It reduces harmful restoration interventions by 54.2% macro and 37.0% pooled while retaining 98.8% of Always-Restore AP, providing useful conditional-perception lineage and a path to skip unnecessary preprocessing.

p1_watchlist.title: MetaKV: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Constrained LLM Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / adaptive compression / constrained inference
p1_watchlist.why: MetaKV predicts latency, peak memory, and correctness for multiple KV compression configurations and selects per-prompt settings under user budgets. Across KVQuant, H2O, RocketKV and FP16 it improves constrained success rate by about 0.07 on average and up to 0.135 over the best static configuration; useful systems direction, but the primary result is budget satisfaction rather than a direct end-to-end speedup, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Streaming Hierarchical Inference with Tabular Foundation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / hierarchical inference / selective offloading
p1_watchlist.why: HINT combines sliding-window graph ANN retrieval at the edge with uncertainty-aware selective offloading to a cloud-hosted tabular foundation model, explicitly trading predictive quality against communication and latency. It is a clean edge-cloud inference pattern, but the current abstract reports favorable trade-offs without concrete throughput/latency gains, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Learning to Fly: Stable Vision-Guided UAV Servoing with Compact Target-Centric Cues and Reinforcement Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / UAV control / compact perception
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces direct high-dimensional RGB policy input with lightweight target segmentation and a compact 12D observation combining image-space cues and proprioception. Protected Physical-AI adaptive-perception lineage; abstract reports robustness rather than measured compute savings.

p1_watchlist.title: ReactVAU: A Slow-Fast Decoupled Framework for Streaming Video Anomaly Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / conditional MLLM invocation / persistent memory
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a slow-fast streaming design where a lightweight detector continuously filters the stream, anomaly-aware persistent memory preserves rare events, and heavyweight MLLM reasoning wakes only on suspicious events. The paper explicitly reports substantially fewer heavyweight MLLM invocations and real-time streaming operation, but the primary abstract omits a single quantitative latency/throughput figure, so it is retained as a high-value serving watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: MicroIntent: Intent-Based Placement Strategy for Microservice Application in the Compute Continuum Using LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compute continuum / LLM placement
p1_watchlist.why: MicroIntent uses LLMs to translate high-level business intent into placement decisions across a geographically distributed compute continuum. It is relevant to cloud-edge orchestration and heterogeneous serving, but current evidence is about placement usability/decision quality rather than AI inference throughput or energy.

p1_watchlist.title: FrogNano: Training a 4B Coding Agent via Online Task Synthesis
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / small coding agents / resource-constrained deployment
p1_watchlist.why: FrogNano trains a 4B coding agent with online task synthesis and reinforcement learning on about 1,500 SWE environments, targeting capable coding agents that can operate under minimal hardware budgets. It is relevant to efficient-agent deployment, but the abstract does not expose a clean latency, memory, or serving-cost reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: JEDI: JEPA-to-Edge Distillation for Efficient Cropland Segmentation from Satellite Imagery
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / distillation / compact vision
p1_watchlist.why: JEDI distills a 639M-parameter I-JEPA teacher into compact 4.04M-28M SegFormer students while preserving much of the task quality. The compression ratio is substantial and deployment-motivated, but the application is remote sensing and the abstract lacks direct latency/energy measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: Interactive Debugger for Performance Portable Python HPC Kernels
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / Python HPC / developer tooling
p1_watchlist.why: PKDB adds breakpoints, stepping, inspection, live code evaluation and hot kernel substitution while preserving on-device PyKokkos execution across CPU/GPU backends. The primary abstract reports limited overhead but no quantified workload speedup; it is retained as high-value runtime/tooling infrastructure.

p1_watchlist.title: Quantization Amplifies Determinism, Not Bias: Scale-Dependent Behavioral Effects of Serving-Time Weight Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM serving / behavioral fidelity
p1_watchlist.why: This controlled serving-time study compares Qwen3 8B/14B/32B under W4A16 AWQ, W8A16 FP8-Marlin and BF16 across about 71k paired completions, finding scale-dependent output concentration and stylistic drift. It is valuable deployment-quality evidence for quantization, but it does not claim a new quantization runtime or measured speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: M3-Tele: A Unified Multimodal Teleoperational Framework for Compliant Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI: M3-Tele is a multimodal whole-body mobile-manipulation teleoperation/data-collection framework that directly targets demonstration efficiency and downstream policy-learning quality.

p1_watchlist.title: The OCUDU dApp Platform: An Open Runtime and E3 Interface for Real-Time AI-RAN
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / real-time AI-RAN / GPU runtime / edge orchestration
p1_watchlist.why: Protected edge/heterogeneous replay recovered an open production-DU runtime that supports GPU-resident receive-chain apps, scheduler-path apps under a 100 us admitted deadline, and never-blocking observer apps. Live GB10 gNB validation shows all three classes running together without fallback. It is highly relevant real-time AI infrastructure, but the abstract does not provide a comparative throughput or speedup baseline, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / long-context / constant-memory recurrent inference
p1_watchlist.why: KDN reformulates recurrent associative memory as a linear-Gaussian state-space model and introduces scan-compatible diagonal and isotropic approximations whose uncertainty recurrences admit associative scans with logarithmic parallel depth. It improves perplexity and downstream accuracy over strong linear-attention baselines, but the abstract does not report measured latency/throughput gains, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Real-Time dApps for AI-RAN: Measured Interface Requirements for Inline PHY and Slot-Level Control
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / AI-RAN / low-latency runtime interface
p1_watchlist.why: This work measures the interface requirements of AI-RAN dApps under live-cell load and shows that only in-process paths continue meeting 100-us control deadlines for bounded/inline workloads once the DU is active. It provides unusually concrete systems measurements and a released ABI, but is adjacent to the core ML-serving focus, so retain as high-value edge-infrastructure watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Signed Rescue Routing: Harm-Aware Cascades for Efficient LLM Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / adaptive compute
p1_watchlist.why: SRR routes requests between Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B by predicting signed incremental gain rather than uncertainty. The method is directly about budgeted efficient inference and uses a lightweight deployment router, but the current abstract still contains TBD quantitative results, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: What Does an LLM-Agent Leaderboard Rank Actually Compare?
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / evaluation / cost-aware benchmarking
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that agent leaderboard conclusions can change with task mixture, measurement source and utility/cost rules, and proposes an estimand-aware pairwise procedure with uncertainty and practical margins. Useful for cost-aware agent-systems evaluation even though it is not itself a runtime optimization.

p1_watchlist.title: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / GUI agents / reproducible runtime evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: APPSim-Bench provides 557 deterministic tasks across 17 simulated real-world apps and explicitly surfaces inefficient trajectories, high action overhead and budget exhaustion across 19 GUI agents. Useful agent-runtime evaluation infrastructure rather than a direct optimization.

p1_watchlist.title: MpSub: A Momentum p-Dimensional Subspace Trust-Region Method for Derivative-Free Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM training efficiency / memory-efficient fine-tuning / zeroth-order optimization
p1_watchlist.why: MpSub targets the activation/gradient memory burden of full-parameter LLM fine-tuning with derivative-free trust-region updates in a low-dimensional subspace and removes per-task learning-rate tuning. Useful training-memory lineage, but the abstract does not provide a clean end-to-end memory or wall-clock ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Accuracy is Not Enough: A Divergence-Based Approach to Evaluate Fidelity Loss in Quantized LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / deployment evaluation / distribution fidelity
p1_watchlist.why: A 120-run matrix across five foundation architectures and four reasoning benchmarks evaluates progressive quantization from BF16 to Q2_K using full-vocabulary JS/TV divergence rather than only argmax accuracy. It shows mixed-precision Q4_K generally preserves distribution fidelity better than Q4_0 at similar memory footprints. This is a useful deployment-quality diagnostic rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Decentralized Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Predictive Shielding
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI: decentralized predictive shielding lets multi-robot policies safely adapt during deployment without centralized coordination; relevant scalable robot runtime lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Same Problem, Different Field: Cross-Domain Solution Import via Domain-Stripped Computational Fingerprints
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Computational fingerprints require one cached LLM distillation call per paper followed by a cheap embedder for cross-domain solution retrieval; useful efficient research-agent/retrieval pipeline lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: ICI-VLA: In-Context Imitation with Spatiotemporally Aligned Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / test-time adaptation / retrieval-conditioned control
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work keeps the VLA fixed at inference and adapts through retrieved phase- and geometry-aligned micro-demonstrations, reaching 97.7% LIBERO, 60.4% RoboTwin 2.0 and 83.2% across four physical tasks. No measured serving latency/throughput benefit is reported, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: No-Regret Mixing of LRU and LFU with Optimal Switching Cost
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / cache policy lineage
p1_watchlist.why: online cache-eviction mixture with regret guarantees and minimum switching cost; relevant cache-policy systems lineage

p1_watchlist.title: SeisBench DAS: A machine learning framework for Distributed Acoustic Sensing
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: SeisBench DAS provides standardized data/model interfaces plus an engine for efficiently applying deep models to diverse large-scale distributed-acoustic-sensing formats; useful ML systems/inference framework evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Heat Kernel Textures: the Geodesic Gaussians That Do Not Splat
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / 3D representation / memory efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Heat Kernel Textures replace UV texture maps with intrinsic anisotropic heat kernels on mesh surfaces, explicitly targeting substantially lower texture-memory footprint while removing UV seams, distortion and wasted space. This is useful representation-efficiency lineage adjacent to Gaussian/3D rendering, but the abstract does not provide a single end-to-end rendering speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Re-engineering SORT-based algorithms for low-cost small object tracking from omnidirectional footage
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / lightweight tracking / CPU inference
p1_watchlist.why: Re-engineers SORT geometry for omnidirectional footage without ReID or transformer appearance encoders; the tracking stage stays CPU-only while improving HOTA/MOTA/IDF1 on the target benchmark.

p1_watchlist.title: Anti-Gravity Walking by a Flying Humanoid Robot via Thrust-Rate Input Whole-Body Model Predictive Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot control / real-time MPC / humanoid
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a real-time whole-body MPC implementation for a flying humanoid, including sparse optimal-control structure and hardware demonstration under contact switching. This is deployment-relevant compute/control evidence, but the abstract does not provide absolute controller latency, throughput, or a comparative runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: PhysReal: Learning Real-World Deformable Object Physics via Hybrid Constitutive Modeling
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models
p1_watchlist.why: hybrid differentiable physics world model

p1_watchlist.title: Functional-SLAM: Interaction-Aware Mapping with Online Functional Scene Graphs
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / online mapping / scene graphs
p1_watchlist.why: Functional-SLAM maintains functional scene graphs online rather than relying on offline reconstruction, with substantially improved runtime while retaining competitive accuracy and enabling topology-assisted loop closure. The lack of concrete latency/throughput values keeps it as a high-value Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: MEMO: Multimodal Evidence Memory Organization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-horizon memory / multimodal evidence budgeting
p1_watchlist.why: Selects relevant evidence blocks and assigns them to textual, visual, or dual-channel carriers under a constrained working-memory budget. Across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, LoCoMo, and ALFWorld it reports fewer memory tokens with improved downstream performance, but the primary abstract gives no exact latency, token-reduction, or cost ratio, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Measuring Language Transfer in Robot Policies: Adding Greek to a Cosmos3 Vision-Language-Action Policy
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / video/image generation acceleration / VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI/VLA: study adds Greek to Cosmos3 VLA and carefully measures multilingual policy transfer, including world-model warm-start and multi-phrasing effects; useful VLA training/evaluation lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Compute-Bounded Security Assurance - Coverage, Verification, and Response under Resource Constraints
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Compute-bounded security assurance formalizes coverage and verification under finite inference budgets and separates repeated attempts from unique coverage; useful compute-budget theory for reasoning/evaluation despite no hardware benchmark.

p1_watchlist.title: Parser-Free VLM Verification for Federated Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / selective inference / federated edge AI
p1_watchlist.why: Trains only a compact MIL scorer across clients and invokes a frozen 2B VLM only on high-scoring suspect segments; next-token Yes/No logits avoid full text generation and parsers. Useful selective-VLM/edge-inference lineage, though system latency is not quantified.

p1_watchlist.title: Open-Set Ego-Noise Separation for Legged-Robot Audition via Annotation-Free Adaptation and Pretrained-Model Transfer
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot sensing / annotation-efficient adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Selects ego-noise-dominant clips from unlabeled robot recordings and adapts a pretrained separator without robot-specific manual labels or separately recorded ego-noise-only data. Protected Physical-AI sensing/adaptation lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Unified Vision-Centric Pedestrian Crossing Action Prediction via Adaptive Patch Projection and Proactive Spatial Rectification
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal token efficiency / autonomous driving
p1_watchlist.why: ViCross targets the cost of high-resolution full-frame MLLM encoding with variable-resolution patch mapping that allocates visual tokens adaptively around pedestrians while preserving target-centric reasoning. This is protected Physical-AI token-efficiency work, but the primary abstract does not provide a reproducible wall-clock or token-reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Think Wider: Mitigating Latent Rank Collapse in Implicit Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / implicit CoT / latent reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: WIDER is a training-time spectral regularizer for implicit CoT that leaves inference decoding unchanged while improving implicit-reasoning baselines and reducing latent redundancy. It targets reasoning efficiency without adding runtime machinery, but the abstract lacks direct latency/token savings.

p1_watchlist.title: OpenWAM: An Open, Modular Exploration Towards Systematic World-Action Model Pretraining
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / WAM infrastructure / deployment stack
p1_watchlist.why: OpenWAM provides an open modular infrastructure that factorizes WAM model, representation, training, inference, deployment and evaluation choices, with released code, checkpoints, data recipes and real-robot evaluation across multiple embodiments. It is important infrastructure for the protected WAM direction, but the paper currently emphasizes modularity, scaling and task performance rather than measured serving speedup, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: A Surrogate-based Approach for Fast Multi-objective Architectural Refactoring Optimization
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: Surrogate-assisted architecture refactoring replaces expensive repeated analysis-tool evaluations and reports up to 30% computational-time savings; useful optimization-system efficiency evidence though not core ML inference.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Fluent Generation: A CPU Reliability Benchmark for MCP-Style Tool Calling in Sub-2B Small Language Models for Edge Deployment
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / tool-using SLMs / CPU inference / reliability-resource tradeoff
p1_watchlist.why: Provides an explicit edge-agent resource baseline for sub-2B tool-calling models. Qwen2.5-1.5B uses 7,960 MiB and 30.782 s mean CPU latency versus 3,637 MiB and 10.627 s for Qwen2.5-0.5B, while reliability changes substantially. This is valuable deployment evidence but a benchmark rather than a new acceleration method, so it stays watch.

p1_watchlist.title: EnvPilot: Systematic Design and Evaluation of an Experience-Augmented Agent for Software Environment Setup
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / software engineering agents / trajectory memory / experience reuse
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains a trajectory-derived memory initialized with 667 validated experiences and retrieves prior setup strategies to avoid redundant exploration. On 112 real GitHub instances across nine languages it reaches 75% Pass@1 while the paper reports reduced reasoning cost, but the primary abstract does not expose a clean quantitative token/latency/cost reduction, so it remains a high-value watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: RouteRelay: Event-Triggered Cross-Layer Route Reuse for Efficient Dynamic Sparse Attention
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / sparse attention / route reuse / GPU kernels
p1_watchlist.why: RouteRelay reuses sparse-attention routing metadata across layers and selectively reroutes rows only when sentinel chunks challenge the retained route. It reaches at least 99.99% route recall and evaluates 38.4-51.6% of full-routing score pairs at larger routing scales, but its current unfused CPU implementation remains slower than dense matrix multiplication, so this is an important systems watch rather than canonical-high yet.

p1_watchlist.title: Long-Horizon Language Model Reinforcement Learning via Progressive Point Matching
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / RL post-training / long-horizon credit assignment
p1_watchlist.why: Segment-level progressive point matching provides an unbiased dense reward and is shown theoretically and empirically to scale exponentially more efficiently than sparse outcome rewards on long-horizon tasks; practical version needs only one reference trajectory per task.

p1_watchlist.title: World Models Under Asynchronous Sensor Observations
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / asynchronous sensing
p1_watchlist.why: Directly studies transformer world models when physical sensor channels arrive at heterogeneous rates. Staleness and time-to-refresh features avoid fabricating interpolated observations or discarding faster sensors, with evaluation in locomotion, MPC and a latched-actuator system. Protected Physical-AI/world-model systems lineage; no direct compute-speedup claim.

p1_watchlist.title: How Long Until Your Robot Ignores You? A Safety Benchmark for LLM Orchestrators in Human-Humanoid Collaboration
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI: benchmark evaluates LLM robot orchestrators over long human-humanoid sessions using simulated sensor-actuator loops and Unitree G1 validation; useful embodied-agent runtime/safety infrastructure.

p1_watchlist.title: Separating Stream Stability from Long-Term Recall in Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / streaming LLM / constant-memory evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: ThreeH separates stability, access and utility horizons under a common state/compute budget and shows that attention-sink streaming can remain stable indefinitely while losing semantic access outside the active cache. It is an important systems-evaluation contract for constant-memory streaming and cache/recurrent/retrieval designs, but it does not introduce a new measured faster runtime, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Matryoshka Hash Representations for Model-Aware Compact Semantic Retrieval
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / RAG retrieval / compact index
p1_watchlist.why: MHR stores documents at one bit per coordinate while supporting directly searchable prefixes at multiple byte budgets and FAISS FastScan. It directly attacks corpus-scale dense-index storage and preserves strong retrieval quality, but does not report end-to-end RAG serving latency.

p1_watchlist.title: Mathematical Modeling of a Cognitive Continuum Digital Shadow for Large-Scale, Cross-Facility Workflows
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / cross-facility scheduling / cost-energy optimization
p1_watchlist.why: The Cognitive Continuum Digital Shadow models cross-facility instruments, networks, storage and compute with stochastic optimization to expose cost, makespan and energy trade-offs before execution. It is relevant heterogeneous-infrastructure scheduling evidence, but this first paper is primarily a mathematical formulation rather than measured AI-serving acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: LightSplat: Real-Time High-Fidelity 3D Gaussian SLAM with Loop Closure
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 3DGS / real-time SLAM
p1_watchlist.why: LightSplat combines sparse tracking with a dual-thread dense Gaussian backend and online loop closure, sustaining about 8 FPS on real-world robotic deployment while preserving reconstruction quality. It is directly relevant real-time 3DGS robotics infrastructure, but stronger comparative speedup evidence is still missing.

p1_watchlist.title: Dense Structural Compression of Transformers via Gauge-Correct Channel Removal
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / dense structural compression / efficient inference
p1_watchlist.why: GaugeLasso learns structurally removable transformer channels while retaining dense tensors suitable for GPU execution, achieving very large FMA compression on controlled tasks and discovering depth-dependent compact architectures. The evidence is scientifically interesting but currently centered on synthetic/statistical tasks without measured LLM-serving latency, so retain as watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Query-Aware Token Budgeting for Efficient Late-Interaction Visual Document Retrieval
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / retrieval systems / token compression
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a heavily compressed hot-path index followed by query-aware stage-two token budgeting over shortlisted pages, recovering 98.39% of full-token score with greedy marginal-gain selection under a pool-factor-eight-equivalent reranking budget. The latency analysis identifies practical operating points but the abstract gives no direct end-to-end speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Phase-and-First-Arrival VLM Feedback for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning in Surgical Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot learning / sparse VLM supervision
p1_watchlist.why: The method uses one VLM query per recorded robot episode to identify the furthest verified task phase and its first arrival time, reusing partial progress for sparse-reward learning. It is valuable Physical-AI supervision-efficiency evidence, but the paper primarily improves learning signal quality rather than inference runtime.

p1_watchlist.title: FedRAW: Preserving Rare-Label Influence in Asynchronous Federated Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / edge AI
p1_watchlist.why: robust asynchronous aggregation under heterogeneous participation

p1_watchlist.title: PhysMAS: Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent Synthesis of Compositional 4D Gaussians
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 4D Gaussian world modeling / physics agents
p1_watchlist.why: PhysMAS uses persistent object-part identity, material reasoning agents and solver-aware skills for physically executable 4D Gaussian synthesis, explicitly avoiding SDS-style repeated score evaluations and backpropagation. It is protected Physical-AI evidence, but the abstract lacks a clean runtime or memory ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Mind the Approximation: Fisher-Weighted SVD Compression for ViTs
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / model compression / vision transformers
p1_watchlist.why: FACTS plus constrained rank search improves ViT accuracy-efficiency under fixed FLOP budgets without finetuning, beating the strongest SVD baseline by up to 5.8 Top-1 points on Swin-B.

p1_watchlist.title: Flow3D-OPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for 3D Geometry Generation with Flow-Matching Diffusion Transformer
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / 3D generation / distillation
p1_watchlist.why: Uses multi-teacher on-policy distillation and hard task routing to consolidate specialized flow-matching 3D teachers into one student while mitigating gradient interference. Relevant flow-distillation lineage; no measured inference acceleration in abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: NutriBench-Kitchen: Benchmarking Embodied AI for Nutrition Management
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / persistent embodied memory / long-horizon kitchen agents
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces 1,500 manually verified QA pairs from 160 cooking videos covering ingredient entry, memory management, recipe query and long/short-term planning, explicitly testing whether embodied agents continuously maintain and use persistent food state. It fills a useful long-horizon memory benchmark gap but does not present serving or runtime-efficiency gains, so it is retained only as protected Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Ollama in the Wild: A Longitudinal Measurement of Exposed Ollama LLM Endpoints at Internet Scale
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / deployment infrastructure / open-source ecosystem
p1_watchlist.why: A 365-day active measurement of self-hosted Ollama endpoints characterizes persistence, upgrade behavior, geography and hosting concentration across roughly 4.8M IP-day observations. It is not an acceleration method, but it is unusually direct systems evidence about real-world open LLM-serving deployment and upgrade behavior.

p1_watchlist.title: Eventually Optimal and Scalable Multi-Agent Planning for Block Cave Mining
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI: SAMMS decomposes autonomous mining fleet planning into short subcycles to trade optimality for scalability while retaining near-optimal throughput; relevant multi-robot planning/runtime lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboDreamer: Anticipatory Humanoid Locomotion with Predictive State-Space Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / humanoid control / action chunking
p1_watchlist.why: RoboDreamer combines predictive state-space modeling, temporal masking/distillation and optional multi-step action chunking for robust humanoid locomotion, with real-time deployment on Unitree G1. The abstract indicates real-time latency but does not quantify serving speedup, so retain as a protected Physical-AI watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Where to Look and What to Use: Retrieve-Localize-Generate for Long-Term Conversational Memory Question Answering
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-term memory / retrieval localization
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces MemLoc, combining multi-granularity memory retrieval, graph-based cross-session routing, and a reasoning-based evidence localizer to reduce noisy long-context evidence before generation. The architecture is directly relevant to efficient long-term agent memory, but the primary abstract does not provide a clean token/latency reduction, so it remains watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: NOVA-CIM: Noise- and Correlation-Tolerant Stochastic Interfaces for Analog Compute-in-Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compute-in-memory / accelerator interfaces
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces multi-bit ADC readout with random-reference 1-bit sensing and lightweight stochastic counting for analog CIM, targeting energy-efficient inference while improving robustness to read noise and correlated stochastic inputs. End-to-end ViT-Base accuracy remains 84.48% versus 84.51% BF16 under modeled read noise, but no measured latency/energy speedup is reported, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: TrojanWorld: Backdooring World-Model Agents via Imagination Steering
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI/WAM: TrojanWorld studies supply-chain attacks on deployed world-model agents across TD-MPC2, DreamerV3 and R2-Dreamer; important WAM deployment/runtime lineage, though not an efficiency mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: Large Discrete Policy: Advancing Explicit Behavior Modeling with Stochastic Iterative Scoring
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / multimodal/MLLM serving / VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI policy design uses discrete candidate actions and iterative score-space pruning instead of continuous denoising; promising efficiency angle but systems evidence is secondary.

p1_watchlist.title: MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot memory / benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark separates robot-memory Storage, Update and Compression across 30 history-dependent tasks, 1,500 demonstrations and 4,200 executable checkpoints; the strongest memory baseline reaches only 31.9% average success. It is important diagnostic infrastructure but not an efficiency-improving runtime, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: GIFT: Goal-Injected Fine-Tuning for Efficient Manipulation Policy Adaptation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / lightweight adaptation / goal-conditioned manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work injects generated goal-image features into pretrained VLA policies through zero-initialized convolution; one epoch of fine-tuning improves reported task success by 4.7-13.4 percentage points. The efficiency claim is adaptation-oriented and the abstract lacks serving/runtime measurements, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: WM-Craftnet: World Synesthesia Model for Generalizable and Robust Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / recurrent world state / dexterous manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a Dreamer-style recurrent world-synesthesia state as a deployable visuotactile estimator for closed-loop dexterous control. Real-robot evidence shows substantial robustness/generalization gains and reusable latent physical structure; protected Physical-AI/world-model lineage, not a direct inference-acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: Continual Learning Mechanisms Compose for Long-Horizon Memorization
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Long-horizon memorization combines data/function/weight anchors with merged LoRA, making continual adaptation parameter-efficient; relevant PEFT/memory lineage despite emphasis on retention rather than systems throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / structured LLM pruning / recovery
p1_watchlist.why: OverRep temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training and algebraically merges it into an inference-time compact module. It improves retained reasoning by up to 5.5 and 8.4 points at 25% and 50% structured pruning while preserving the compact deployed architecture, but current evidence emphasizes quality recovery rather than measured latency, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: PRG-Fusion: Orchestrating Generative Priors with Reconstruction Evidence for Driving View Synthesis
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / simulation / region-adaptive generation
p1_watchlist.why: Routes regions among 3DGS preservation, LiDAR-guided repair, and video-prior generation according to reconstruction evidence. Protected Physical-AI simulation lineage with explicit region-adaptive compute semantics; current abstract emphasizes quality rather than latency.

p1_watchlist.title: Unified AI Gateway: A Framework for Joint Model Routing and KV Cache Management
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / KV cache management / edge-cloud placement
p1_watchlist.why: Unified AI Gateway jointly reasons about model choice, execution site, and KV-cache actions under quality, latency, cost and resource constraints, with analytical workload simulations reporting 1.25-13.28x TTFT and 1.20-6.16x input-cost benefits. It is strategically relevant but is primarily a synthesis/framework with simulation rather than a new measured deployed system, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Distributed Dexterous Manipulation with Spatially Conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multi-agent transformer / dexterous manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work uses spatially conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers for an 8x8 array of 64 soft delta robots and introduces action selection that maintains real-world manipulation accuracy around 1.5 cm while using about 65% fewer robots. This is meaningful resource-use evidence, but the primary abstract does not report inference latency/throughput or compute speedup, so it remains watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: BEFORE THE FLIP: Measuring Hidden Score Shifts In Quantized Vision Language Models Before The Answer Changes for Visual Question Answering
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / multimodal VLM / evaluation methodology
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that 4-bit compression can materially shift VLM answer margins even when discrete answers remain unchanged, while per-question mixed-precision selection fails to beat shuffled controls at tested storage budgets. Useful evidence that VLM quantization evaluation should inspect hidden score movement rather than answer flips alone, but it does not introduce a new acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Learning Adaptive SED for heterogeneous load balancing
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / scheduling lineage
p1_watchlist.why: online learning of heterogeneous service rates with finite-regret shortest-expected-delay routing; useful scheduling/load-balancing theory lineage

p1_watchlist.title: Contextual Observer Grounding: Evaluating Situated Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark for contextual observer grounding tests situated spatial reasoning from multi-view embodied observations; capability-side protected lineage, not direct systems efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving / multi-tenant security characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Seven experiments on live shared LLM serving show that KV-cache timing side-channel reliability collapses under realistic contention; on a two-node two-GPU tensor-parallel vLLM setup mean effect size drops from 3.418 to 0.511. This is valuable multi-tenant KV-cache systems characterization rather than an efficiency-improving runtime, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: BinauralVAE: Spatial Audio Reconstruction For World Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal world models
p1_watchlist.why: Open-source binaural representation pipeline couples robot navigation with spatialized acoustic consequences, adding an audio-centric state channel for world models under visual occlusion or poor lighting. Protected Physical-AI world-model lineage; no inference-efficiency metric yet.

p1_watchlist.title: Constrained Bayesian Optimization for Hierarchical Federated Learning in IoT Networks for Plant Disease Classification
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: Constrained Bayesian optimization explicitly co-optimizes model architecture, federation strategy and communication rounds under energy/time/accuracy constraints in resource-constrained IoT HFL; useful edge training-efficiency lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Diagnosing and Dynamically Filtering Occupancy World Models for Active Mapping
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world-model runtime / active mapping / occupancy filtering
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI/world-model work that isolates how occupancy completion errors alter both exploration choices and motion feasibility, then studies dynamic filtering of learned occupancy for active mapping. The planner is held fixed so the effect of the world-model representation is attributable, making this useful for world-model runtime reliability and selective-use policies. It does not present a direct serving or compute speedup metric in the primary abstract, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: BLINK: Batch Normalization-based Integrity Checkpoints for In-Situ Detection and Mitigation of Diverse Weight Corruptions in DNN Accelerators
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / accelerator reliability / runtime
p1_watchlist.why: BLINK performs autonomous on-chip inference-time corruption detection and mitigation without host intervention or fine-tuning data, with >99% detection precision and under 2% latency overhead. It is valuable accelerator-runtime resilience work but not primarily an efficiency contribution, so retain as watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Reason Through the Latent! Making Latent Visual Reasoning Necessary
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / multimodal/MLLM serving / video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: CVRR removes visual states and the original multimodal KV cache before decoding so the final recurrent state alone carries image-conditioned information; useful multimodal/KV-interface lineage, but no explicit latency or memory benchmark is reported.

p1_watchlist.title: Event Interaction in Low-Rank Bottlenecks for Temporal Relation Extraction
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: CBI improves LoRA/adapter temporal-relation models with lightweight depthwise convolution and multiplicative interaction inside low-rank bottlenecks, adding minimal computational cost; retain as parameter-efficient adaptation lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Companion-style QA Assistance in Ego-Vision
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / streaming video memory / egocentric agents
p1_watchlist.why: BuddyVQA targets long-form egocentric streaming QA; MyBuddy adds a question filter and multi-level memory specifically to make QA and visual retrieval efficient in streaming settings. Protected Physical-AI/MLLM runtime lineage, but no explicit token or latency reduction is reported.

p1_watchlist.title: A Grapheme-Aware Indic Tokenizer for Tamil: Large-Scale Training and Intrinsic Evaluation
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: Grapheme-aware tokenizer explicitly targets sequence-length and computational-cost inefficiency in Tamil tokenization; retain as tokenizer/sequence-efficiency lineage pending downstream serving measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: Data Efficient Sample Selection for In-Context Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / in-context learning / sample selection
p1_watchlist.why: DearICL models demonstration selection as subset ranking and reports 8.08-15.9% accuracy gains over linear-bandit baselines with low sample complexity. It is relevant to efficient prompt/demo selection, although the abstract does not quantify prompt-token or wall-clock savings.

p1_watchlist.title: ECOKV: Geometry-Aware KV Cache Eviction via Complementary Diversity Metrics
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / multimodal MLLM serving / cache eviction
p1_watchlist.why: Directly relevant KV-cache compression work for multimodal LLMs: complementary Euclidean and cosine diversity metrics estimate per-head redundancy and adaptively balance diversity and importance while reducing the recent-token observation window. The primary abstract reports state-of-the-art quality across compression ratios but no measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or memory-speedup number, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Multi-History-Step SDE Inversion for Image Editing with Superior Regional Awareness
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / image editing / low-step sampling
p1_watchlist.why: Predictor-corrector multi-history-step SDE inversion targets faithful editing with fewer sampling steps and automatic semantic masks without extra user input. Direct diffusion sampling-efficiency mechanism, but abstract does not quantify wall-clock speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Unifying Physics-Based Humanoid Interaction with a Context-Conditioned Interaction Prior
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / humanoid control / reusable skill prior
p1_watchlist.why: Distills heterogeneous locomotion/manipulation teachers into a shared context-conditioned interaction prior that is reused and adapted for downstream humanoid tasks. Protected Physical-AI modular-policy lineage; no clean inference-speed claim.

p1_watchlist.title: Assessing Fixed-Batch Reporting for Deadline-constrained Inference in Intermittently Powered IoT
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
p1_watchlist.why: Deadline-constrained intermittent inference study gives an explicit analytical trade-off between communication actions, retained state, energy and latency under batching; useful edge-inference systems lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Learning to Use Imagination: Progress-Conditioned Future Utilization for World Action Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world action models / adaptive imagination
p1_watchlist.why: ProWAM explicitly models execution progress and uses hierarchical progress-conditioned modulation to vary how imagined future latents are consumed across stages and within a stage. This is directly relevant to adaptive WAM runtime design and avoids treating every imagined future as equally useful, although the abstract reports quality rather than compute savings.

p1_watchlist.title: 3DHarnessBench: Probing Agentic 3D-to-Code Capabilities of Frontier Vision-Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agentic 3D tool use / benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: Benchmarks frontier VLM agents from passive views through active visual exploration to full Blender function-call interaction, exposing model-dependent gains from richer tool access. Useful agent-harness/tool-use evaluation lineage, though it does not report systems-efficiency savings.

p1_watchlist.title: VLA-Corrector: Stage-Aware Observable State Understanding for Prompt-Based Closed-Loop Recovery of Vision-Language-Action Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / closed-loop recovery / runtime verifier
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work adds an observable-history Learned Verifier over multi-view vision, proprioception and executed actions, then produces stage-conditioned recovery prompts for the same frozen VLA policy without privileged simulator state. LIBERO and LIBERO Plus evaluations show substantially improved closed-loop reliability, but no measured serving overhead or throughput is reported in the primary abstract, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: DFlow: Enabling Verifier Information Flow in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
p1_watchlist.topic: speculative decoding / diffusion language models / verifier reuse
p1_watchlist.why: DFlow reuses verifier hidden states from rejected suffix positions across drafting rounds, so spent verifier computation informs later drafts without extra target computation, and self-conditioning teaches that cross-round information flow. It improves draft quality and acceptance length over DFlash on Qwen3, but the primary abstract gives no exact end-to-end throughput or latency speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: One MLLM, One Call: Efficient Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation via Spatial-Aware Waypoints
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / VLN / sparse MLLM invocation / robot navigation
p1_watchlist.why: O2C-Nav reduces zero-shot VLN-CE to a single MLLM call per decision step using structured waypoints, explicit spatial markers, and a low-level FMM planner, directly targeting inference latency and visual-processing overhead. It outperforms prior zero-shot methods and releases code, but the current primary abstract does not provide hard end-to-end latency/throughput numbers, so retain as protected high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Steering Under Compression: Dose-Response, Capability Cost, and Failure Asymmetry in Quantized LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM deployment / activation steering / capability-cost characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Systematically studies inference-time activation steering under INT8 and NF4 across four open 7-9B models. It finds steering directions largely survive compression but capability-cost and failure behavior change substantially, including a Mistral-NF4 GSM8K baseline shift from 0.545 to 0.365. Valuable deployment characterization, but not a new acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: PACO: A Fully Cache-Oblivious Parallel FFT with One Global Redistribution
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / parallel FFT / communication-efficient HPC
p1_watchlist.why: PACO fuses deferred cache-oblivious layout changes into the single redistribution already required by the parallel FFT, proving optimal local cache complexity and exactly one global redistribution round under its ownership model. The current paper is primarily theoretical and exposes no measured end-to-end hardware speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: PLSR: Progressive and Localized Super-Resolution of 3D Objects via Localized Latent Voxel Diffusion
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / 3D generation / localized denoising / memory efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Decomposes global 3D super-resolution into localized latent-voxel diffusion subproblems with low-cost finetuning and patch-wise denoising, explicitly targeting memory and computational efficiency for high-resolution 3D generation. The primary abstract claims significant computational-cost reduction but gives no exact speedup or memory number, so it is kept as a high-value diffusion-efficiency watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Stability and Generalization of Straight-Through Estimators for Training Two-Layer Quantized Neural Networks
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization
p1_watchlist.why: theoretical stability/generalization lineage for STE-based binary activation training; relevant to low-bit quantization methodology

p1_watchlist.title: OVMAN: A Task and Benchmark for Open-Vocabulary Motion-Aware Navigation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / persistent scene memory / navigation
p1_watchlist.why: Two-visit navigation benchmark requires reasoning about moved, removed and former object locations. Existing open-vocabulary systems fail badly on vacated-location queries, directly exposing persistent scene-memory debt relevant to streaming Physical-AI agents.

p1_watchlist.title: From Concentration to Differentiation and Back: Routing Effective Rank in MoE Reasoning Cohorts
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / efficient reasoning / routing characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces routing effective rank as a label-free measure of cross-rollout MoE expert-routing organization during test-time scaling, with a reproducible low-high-low trajectory across ten MoE configurations and five reasoning benchmarks. This is useful systems characterization for dynamic routing and test-time compute policies, but it does not itself provide a serving speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Worst-Case Coreset Bounds for $k$-Clustering via Determinantal Sampling
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving
p1_watchlist.why: Determinantal sampling constructs smaller clustering coresets under natural data assumptions, providing principled memory/compute reduction lineage even though it is not specific to modern foundation-model systems.

p1_watchlist.title: Linear Algebra Foundations of Efficient Attention: A Phase Reversal in Rank Collapse Under SVD Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / low-rank compression / KV-cache lineage
p1_watchlist.why: Unifies low-rank attention/KV-cache compression literature and adds a controlled finding that SVD compression reverses its rank-collapse behavior between initialization and pretrained models. Useful compression-mechanism lineage, but it does not present a direct serving latency/throughput improvement, so it stays watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: One Shared LoRA Weight for MRI Reconstruction across Acceleration Factors
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient training/inference / parameter-efficient adaptation / shared LoRA
p1_watchlist.why: Uses one shared LoRA adapter set plus a lightweight gate across multiple acceleration factors instead of maintaining separate models, with trainable parameters reported at only about 5% of the backbone while retaining competitive reconstruction quality. Useful parameter/storage-efficiency evidence, but domain-specific and without a direct serving speedup claim.

p1_watchlist.title: Geometric Distributional Control: Learning Progress with Partial Structural Knowledge
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-time control / partial-model planning
p1_watchlist.why: GDC factorizes real-time control into a known feasibility scaffold plus a learned local progress signal, avoiding full global Bellman recursion or a fully specified online planner. Protected Physical-AI control/runtime lineage; experiments show effectiveness but the abstract lacks direct latency or compute savings.

p1_watchlist.title: Query-Oblivious Coresets for Softmax Attention: Improved Bounds and Efficient Constructions
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / attention coresets / theory
p1_watchlist.why: Constructs query-oblivious subsets of key-value pairs that approximate softmax attention uniformly over a query ball, improving coreset-size bounds and giving randomized polynomial-time constructions. This is directly relevant to principled attention compression, but current evidence is theoretical rather than measured accelerator/runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Object-Aware Background-Controlled Editing via Weighted Velocity Guidance
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / training-free image-video editing
p1_watchlist.why: OAVC performs object-localized velocity control directly during diffusion/rectified-flow inference with no retraining or base-model modification. It is relevant inference-time flow-control lineage, but the reported improvements are fidelity/stability rather than wall-clock acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: IM-ENGINE: Image Editing for Embodied Data Generation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embodied data generation / simulation
p1_watchlist.why: Uses image editing as an intermediate representation, then recovers simulator-grounded 3D state and physics-valid robot supervision for grasping and goal-state generation. It offers a scalable alternative to costly human demonstrations and is relevant to embodied training-data efficiency, but the primary abstract provides no direct runtime acceleration metric.

p1_watchlist.title: SIDE: Sensor Impersonation Detection at the Edge via Sequence Prediction
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / edge inference / quantization / tiny ML
p1_watchlist.why: Deploys an LSTM detector on Arduino Nano 33 BLE and compares non-quantized, 16-bit, and 8-bit variants: model size falls from 554 KB to 298.5 KB and 185 KB, while the authors explicitly report quantization made execution slower in their measurements. This is a useful hardware-aware negative result for edge quantization, not a strong acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: MobileVLA-R1 2.0: RL-Enhanced Reasoning for Mobile Robot Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / mobile robot control / reasoning-action decoupling
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work coupling structured embodied reasoning with a reasoning-conditioned action decoder and embodiment-specific controllers, evaluated on navigation, quadruped control and real Unitree Go2/G1 deployments. It improves task success but reports no serving/runtime efficiency metric, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: RefGuard: Identity-Aware Language-Guided Robot Manipulation via Joint Target-Anchor-Frame Grounding
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / deployment reliability / grounding / robot runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains a joint target-anchor-reference-frame posterior and defers execution when grounding is ambiguous. On a real UF850 arm it records zero identity switches on ambiguity-stress trials and 90.0% correct execution versus 33-46% identity-switch rates for baselines; protected deployment-reliability work rather than a compute acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: EgoNeMo: Transferable Map of Pedestrian Dynamics via Egocentric LiDAR Scan
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / navigation / transferable scene dynamics
p1_watchlist.why: Infers a transferable continuous map of pedestrian dynamics in unseen environments from a single instantaneous egocentric LiDAR scan, avoiding site-specific trajectory accumulation. Protected Physical-AI world-state lineage; efficiency benefit is data/observation reuse rather than measured inference speed.

p1_watchlist.title: From Splats to Silicon: Rethinking Computational Efficiency of 3DGS
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / 3DGS acceleration / accelerator architecture
p1_watchlist.why: This workload-centric 3DGS systems study connects representation changes, GPU runtime optimization and hardware architecture, with reproduced measurements and controlled GPU profiling that trace workload counts into stage time and memory traffic. It is highly relevant to efficient-3DGS systems methodology, but its contribution is synthesis and characterization rather than a single new faster runtime, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Rethinking One-Shot Federated Graph Learning: Training-Free Statistical Estimation
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / training-free learning / communication efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: SPEAR removes local GNN training entirely for one-shot federated graph learning and reports at least an order-of-magnitude speedup over all baselines, reaching several orders over generative/distillation methods. Strong efficiency evidence, but the workload is specialized graph FL rather than core foundation-model infra.

p1_watchlist.title: Compressed Recurrent Feedback in Tsetlin Machines: A Reproducible Boolean-FSM Study
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compact recurrent inference
p1_watchlist.why: Compresses 480 clause activations to 96 recurrent bits while keeping accuracy within about one point of raw feedback; raw feedback increases measured host execution time by 4.38x and 3.71x. The no-feedback control is competitive, so this is useful edge-inference evidence but not a strong canonical result.

p1_watchlist.title: Protocol Compression Changes Which Party Pays: Bilateral Cost in Cross-Organization LLM Agent Communication
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent communication / protocol compression / token cost
p1_watchlist.why: Measures bilateral token and monetary cost of compressed protocols across six vendors and 1,053 completed cross-organization agent dialogues. Negotiated sessions cost 52% of the English baseline largely because they terminate sooner, while break-even horizons are 20-70 turns and some vendor pairs reverse which endpoint is cheaper. Valuable deployment economics and communication-efficiency evidence, but not a generally positive acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Where Success Breaks: Failure-Boundary Learning for Robust Vision-Language-Action Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / robust adaptation / failure recovery
p1_watchlist.why: Frames robust VLA adaptation as discovering, localizing, and shaping failure boundaries rather than only fitting successful demonstrations. DLS uses real-grounded priors plus simulated co-training to expose recovery boundaries; retained as a protected deployment-robustness watch item because the main contribution is reliability rather than measured serving efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: DataFlex-RL: An Evaluation Platform for RLVR Data Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / RLVR training systems / data efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: DataFlex-RL evaluates 13 RLVR data-policy configurations under a common GRPO recipe and finds no reproducible gain over uniform sampling at matched precision. This is useful negative systems evidence for avoiding unnecessary rollout-selection complexity in reasoning post-training.

p1_watchlist.title: FANS: Federated Adaptive Network Search Learning for Heterogeneous Devices
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / federated learning / elastic models
p1_watchlist.why: Learns a shared architecture space for heterogeneous clients rather than a tiny fixed model menu, expanding feasible subnetworks by orders of magnitude and improving accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and BERT workloads.

p1_watchlist.title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive layer routing / cached VLM representations
p1_watchlist.why: LayerRoute dynamically mixes cached VLM-layer representations and rereads prior action states for VLA control, improving StarVLA-pi and pi0.5 across simulation and real-world benchmarks with only 0.31%/3.87% added parameters. It is highly relevant to adaptive representation access and cache reuse, but the current evidence emphasizes task quality rather than measured inference speedup, so retain as protected high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Retraining-Free MoE Compression: A Cost-Normalized Study of Post-Compression Adjustment
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / compression / deployment memory / adjustment cost
p1_watchlist.why: This study evaluates four MoE pruning/merging methods on two MoE LLM backbones with matched GPU-cost accounting and shows that a tiny one-epoch post-compression adjustment on 3,000 C4 examples recovers 37.3% of the original-to-compressed performance gap on average. It is useful deployment-efficiency evidence, but it does not provide a new serving runtime or measured latency/throughput speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: NSFlow: End-to-End Differentiable Neuro-Symbolic Optical Flow for Visual Odometry
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embedded visual odometry / realtime perception / efficient robotics
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a hybrid CNN plus differentiable Lucas-Kanade optical-flow front-end that is explicitly designed for efficient VO/VIO and reports realtime embedded deployment with lower latency than purely regression-based alternatives. The abstract does not expose a directly comparable absolute latency or speedup figure, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: SCoCaT: Success Conditioned Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Spacecraft Docking
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI: termination-based constrained RL avoids online optimization at inference and is validated on spacecraft and sim-to-real robotic platforms; useful low-overhead control-inference lineage though the paper is primarily safety/control.

p1_watchlist.title: DAREBench: Deployment-Aware and Reliable Evaluation of Models as Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / deployment benchmark / cost-aware model selection
p1_watchlist.why: DAREBench evaluates 35 commercial and local models over 7,587 agent runs and reports accuracy, token consumption and API reference cost across a workload matrix. It is valuable for deployment-aware agent quality-cost selection, but is primarily a benchmark rather than an acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: SkillSpec: Intent-Masked Specification Reasoning for Agent Skill Correctness
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / reusable skills / agent infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: SkillSpec treats reusable agent skills as specification-bearing artifacts, checks heterogeneous skill repositories under controlled context masks, and validates defects in an isolated sandbox. On 515 real-world skills it finds 763 confirmed defects across 239 skills. Important reusable-skill infrastructure lineage, albeit quality assurance rather than acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: FALCON-S: Fixed-wing ground-effect Aerodynamics Simulator and Flight Control Learning Suite
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / GPU simulation / robot learning
p1_watchlist.why: FALCON-S provides modular high-fidelity 6DoF fixed-wing ground-effect simulation with CPU and NVIDIA Warp GPU backends and high-throughput parallel execution for RL and optimal-control rollouts. It is valuable Physical-AI simulation infrastructure, but the abstract gives no comparative throughput figures.

p1_watchlist.title: Generator-Independent Runtime Assurance under Partial Observation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / runtime assurance
p1_watchlist.why: generator-independent runtime safety gate for learned policies and LM planners

p1_watchlist.title: GLoRI: Closed-Loop Whole-Body Tracking with Global-Local Reference Interaction for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / humanoid control / closed-loop runtime
