p1_watchlist.why: Closed-loop global-local controller reaches 100% held-out HuMoTo completion and transfers Isaac Gym to MuJoCo without fine-tuning, then runs a single real Unitree G1 policy over unseen objects. Protected Physical-AI runtime lineage without explicit inference-cost gains.

p1_watchlist.title: MOAE: Multi-Objective Agent Evolution with Pareto-Preserving Search
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / rollout-budget optimization / Pareto search
p1_watchlist.why: MOAE performs parameter-free in-context agent evolution while preserving non-dominated rollouts under a limited rollout budget, explicitly including efficiency among deployment objectives. It is relevant to cost-aware agent construction, but the abstract lacks direct token/API/latency savings.

p1_watchlist.title: A Brain-inspired Hierarchical Framework for Zero-Shot Robot Task Reasoning and Execution
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hierarchical robot reasoning / closed-loop execution
p1_watchlist.why: The framework decomposes robot reasoning into perception/state inference, language grounding, reusable atomic actions, cost-based plan selection, and refreshed-observation verification, outperforming ReKep, Dream2Flow and pi0.5 on tested tasks. It is valuable Physical-AI system lineage but provides no measured inference/runtime efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: Efficient and Robust Camera-independent Multiview 3D Geometric Reconstruction from Noisy Monocular Depth Estimation and Multiple Point Matching
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / efficient 3D perception / camera-independent reconstruction
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a camera-independent linear geometric autoregression matrix learned from multi-frame point correspondences; can exploit fast-but-noisy monocular depth and avoids camera-pose recovery. Useful lightweight 3D-perception lineage, but the abstract gives no end-to-end latency or FLOP reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: LoGIC: Budgeted Context Construction for Node-Level Graph In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / efficient attention / context budgeting / graph in-context learning
p1_watchlist.why: LoGIC targets the quadratic attention, preprocessing, and memory bottlenecks caused by using the full labeled training table as graph-ICL context. It allocates labeled-context and unlabeled-halo budgets, shares context within graph-local query clusters, and reports markedly lower peak memory while preserving locally runnable full-context performance and enabling frozen graph ICL on million-node graphs. The primary abstract lacks an exact latency or memory-reduction factor, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Efficiency Methods for Multi-Agent Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent efficiency / evaluation methodology
p1_watchlist.why: Directly audits claimed efficiency gains in LLM multi-agent systems under a shared backbone, agent registry, runtime, topology, scale, depth, and tool-use controls. It shows that apparent gains can come from structural collapse, disabled tool pathways, or weak starting systems where random pruning already preserves accuracy. This is important for evaluating agent-efficiency papers, but it is primarily a diagnostic benchmark rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: AVSplat: Dense-View Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Assist-View Preconditioning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 3D perception / feed-forward 3DGS
p1_watchlist.why: Uses one lightweight interaction with a small relevance/diversity-selected Assist-View set before global attention, plus occupancy-aware voxel fusion, restoring positive scaling as input views grow. Relevant efficient 3D perception lineage, though abstract lacks wall-clock savings.

p1_watchlist.title: PAI-Actor: Cinematic Multi-Character Replacement in Dynamic Scenes
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / autoregressive distillation / long-form generation
p1_watchlist.why: PAI-Actor distills a high-quality bidirectional diffusion transformer into an autoregressive video-to-video model for more efficient long-form 1080P generation. The systems direction is directly relevant, but the abstract does not provide concrete latency, throughput, or FLOP reductions.

p1_watchlist.title: Neuron-Guided Fine-Tuning: Unlocking Efficient Alignment Mechanisms for Large Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization/sparsity/pruning / parameter-efficient LLM fine-tuning / activation-guided updates
p1_watchlist.why: NGFT uses activation patterns to select task-relevant neurons in one forward pass, select information-dense data, and align activations to pretrained states, explicitly targeting parameter redundancy and fine-tuning efficiency. The abstract claims efficiency gains but gives no concrete compute, memory or wall-clock ratio, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: FreeTransformSR: Efficient Lightweight Image Super-Resolution via Free Low-Rank Learnable Transform
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / lightweight image restoration
p1_watchlist.why: FreeTransformSR reports 595K parameters, significantly fewer FLOPs, and faster inference than competing super-resolution methods while preserving competitive quality. It is useful lightweight vision-generation evidence, but the abstract lacks a clean common-platform speedup ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: UniRRM: Unified Reasoning Reward Models Across Languages and Evaluation Paradigms
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems
p1_watchlist.why: UniRRM targets costly proprietary LLM-as-a-Judge dependence with unified 8B/14B multilingual reasoning reward models across pairwise/listwise evaluation; useful compact evaluator lineage, but the abstract does not quantify inference savings.

p1_watchlist.title: From Narrative to Auditable Forecasts: A Structured Scaffold for Agentic Forecasting
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive scaffold / cost-aware inference
p1_watchlist.why: AuditForecast replaces unstructured narrative aggregation with a quantitative baseline, targeted retrieval and mechanical odds-space updates. Across live forecasting benchmarks it improves accuracy/calibration and outperforms substantially more expensive deep-research agents while remaining Pareto-dominant in the cost-accuracy tradeoff. Useful agent-system evidence, but the abstract does not expose a single reproducible latency or dollar-cost reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Broken on Arrival: Silently Defective LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / deployment reliability / model registry QA
p1_watchlist.why: Execution-based auditing of 327 quantized GGUF artifacts finds silently defective official and community conversions that surface heuristics miss, and releases a quantized-model acceptance-testing tool. This is deployment QA rather than acceleration but is important low-bit infra lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Map the Possibilities: Spatial Belief Fields for Language-Goal Aerial Navigation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / closed-loop navigation / spatial memory
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains a task-conditioned spatial belief field and updates it online from partial observations rather than collapsing to one waypoint; on unseen CityNav it improves SPL from 19.63% to 30.43%. Protected Physical-AI lineage, but it is an effectiveness result rather than an inference-efficiency paper.

p1_watchlist.title: Learning Counterfactual World Models for Embodied Reasoning under Partial Observability
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / planning
p1_watchlist.why: Counterfactual Latent World Models explicitly separate intervention outcomes under partial observability, improving planning success and reducing exploitative planning failures; the counterfactual-separability metric strongly tracks planning success. Protected world-model lineage, but not a compute optimization.

p1_watchlist.title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal MoE / reactive control
p1_watchlist.why: CR-VLA-Force explicitly targets the latency and action-chunk limitations of force-aware VLA control using a multimodal MoE plus VLA-guided adaptive compliance controller, and validates on real contact-rich tasks. It is accepted by IEEE RA-L and highly relevant to reactive Physical-AI deployment, but the current primary abstract does not provide measured end-to-end latency or throughput numbers, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Scaling Optimal Classification Trees via Adaptive Feature and Sample Reduction
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/algorithm systems
p1_watchlist.why: feature/sample reduction for exact-tree optimization; reported up to 121.41x solver speedup

p1_watchlist.title: Spillover-Aware Multi-Value Steering for Pluralistic LLM Alignment
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / activation steering / inference-time control
p1_watchlist.why: Derives a zero-cost geometric correction that decouples simultaneous activation-steering directions, requiring no fine-tuning, reward model, or manual prompt engineering. Relevant inference-time behavioral-control lineage, though the paper optimizes steering fidelity rather than serving latency.

p1_watchlist.title: Dynamic Lagging for Simultaneous Translation
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / efficient reasoning / latency-controlled generation
p1_watchlist.why: Fine-tunes Qwen3-8B for prefix-aware simultaneous translation and uses a single training-free confidence threshold to trace a continuous quality-latency frontier that outperforms wait-k and suffix-deletion controls. This is directly relevant to latency-aware LLM decoding, though the abstract does not report a universal wall-clock speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Bird's-Eye-View Maps from Cross-View Transformers as Inputs to Behavior-Cloning Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / closed-loop perception-policy interface / autonomous driving
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI systems evidence: evaluates predicted BEV representations as direct policy inputs and shows aggregate perception metrics can diverge from closed-loop task success, identifying route-channel quality as the actual policy bottleneck. Valuable representation/runtime evaluation lineage, not an acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for On-Device Fire Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge inference / VLM distillation
p1_watchlist.why: This work distills domain-specialized VLMs into compact students and deploys them on a commercial Detectium fire sensor, jointly measuring reasoning accuracy, latency and memory. It is valuable real-device MLLM deployment evidence, but the abstract does not report a concrete speedup or latency reduction, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Inference-Time Graph Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent orchestration / inference-time workflow graphs
p1_watchlist.why: ReActNet compiles each query into task-conditioned temporal communication graphs with edge-level message semantics, separating graph compilation from execution without RL or gradient-based topology optimization. It improves multiple reasoning and assistant tasks while maintaining competitive inference cost, but the abstract gives no exact cost or latency reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: RAPTOR: Role-Aware Private Training for Mixture-of-Experts
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / distributed training / private fine-tuning
p1_watchlist.why: RAPTOR separates shared and expert optimization, uses expert-specific clipping/noise, and exploits parallel privacy composition across routed experts. It gives consistent utility gains on Switch Transformer, OLMoE and DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny under matched privacy budgets, but the abstract does not quantify training-time or memory savings.

p1_watchlist.title: RAGMark: A Comprehensive Framework for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / RAG systems / benchmarking
p1_watchlist.why: RAGMark is a modular multi-GPU RAG benchmark collecting per-stage latency, TTFT, throughput, GPU utilization, memory, power and quality. Its experiments expose cross-stage bottleneck shifts and show reranking plus compression can lower energy by up to 66%, but the contribution is primarily measurement infrastructure rather than a new serving mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: WIP: Energy-Efficient LLM-Based Serving Cluster Formulation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / LLM agent resource control / wireless energy efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Uses an LLM-based agent to formulate serving clusters in a simulated cell-free massive-MIMO network and reports up to 32% energy-efficiency gain over the baseline. Relevant to AI-native edge/network resource control, but it is a work-in-progress networking application rather than core ML serving infrastructure, so it remains watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Scalar Flexibility: From Eligible AI Workloads to Dependable Load Relief
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / datacenter power / workload flexibility
p1_watchlist.why: Reconstructs 4,439 hourly power observations from a 185-day trace of 155,410 GPUs and derives duration/reliability-aware AI workload flexibility. Valuable production-scale AI-infrastructure power characterization, but not an ML acceleration technique.

p1_watchlist.title: What Matters, When? Diagnosing and Improving Conditional Visual Grounding in Visuomotor Imitation Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / visuomotor grounding / robustness
p1_watchlist.why: Systematically localizes distractor failures to phase-conditional target selection in ACT and a pretrained VLA policy, then tests augmentation, attention regularization and visual prompting on simulation and a physical UR3e. It is useful Physical-AI runtime/robustness lineage, but does not report inference speed or compute reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Procedural Reasoning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / long-horizon VLA / procedural memory
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work combining learned VLA control with explicit task graphs and multimodal procedural memory to maintain long-horizon task state, dependencies, conditional branches and visual evidence. It is an ECCV 2026 workshop extended abstract and does not report compute-side speedup, so it is retained as a high-value watch for VLA runtime/state architecture rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Design Docs Are All You Need: An AI-native Machine-Learning Performance Tool
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / ML performance modeling / agentic tooling
p1_watchlist.why: SMART stores a DAG of design documents and uses coding agents to regenerate an ML-system performance-modeling library as hardware/model assumptions change. It is relevant AI-infra tooling for rapidly evolving accelerator/software stacks, but it is a performance-modeling workflow rather than a direct inference/training acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: MEOX: Compact Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts for Earth Observation
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / compact multimodal MoE / parameter efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: MEOX combines modality adapters, validity signals, sparse experts, low-rank residuals, and rotary attention in a 2.939M-parameter encoder while achieving strong frozen-transfer results. The workload is Earth observation, but the architecture is a useful compact multimodal-MoE efficiency datapoint; no direct serving latency or energy result is given.

p1_watchlist.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory portability / RAG migration
p1_watchlist.why: Controlled migration study shows fixed-schema KG memory transfers almost unchanged, compressed notes are highly model-coupled, and half-migrated embedding indexes forfeit most of the gain from full re-embedding. Important systems evidence for durable agent-memory formats and migration cost.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboSPA: Can VLA Models Go Beyond Simple Scenes and Short-Horizon Tasks?
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / benchmark / long-horizon embodied reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark with 10 task categories, 56 base tasks, 280 difficulty variants and 527K trajectories across multiple embodiments. It exposes spatial, execution, and memory-intensive planning failures in current VLAs and provides official data/code, but it is primarily a diagnostic benchmark rather than an efficiency/runtime contribution, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Adaptive Gated Deepfake Detection for Low-Resolution and Resource-Constrained Environments
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / adaptive inference / early exit
p1_watchlist.why: AdaGate-DF routes samples through a dual multi-exit path using image-quality cues so easier inputs can exit early, targeting resource-constrained inference while maintaining competitive detection accuracy. The abstract reports low latency but no clean speedup ratio, so it remains a watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Human-Human & Human-Robot Interaction Transformer (H2INT) for Robot Navigation in Dense and Uncertain Crowds
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot navigation / interaction modeling
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a gated Transformer and recurrent policy to model human-human and human-robot interactions under heterogeneous pedestrian responsiveness. It is a useful Physical-AI navigation and temporal-interaction lineage point, but it does not establish inference acceleration or deployment-efficiency gains in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / RLVR post-training / self-distillation
p1_watchlist.why: RISE constructs a synthetic teacher directly from the model own RLVR trajectory and refreshes it every iteration, eliminating an external teacher or privileged conditioning while converting sparse outcome rewards into dense token-level targets. Strong reasoning-post-training efficiency lineage, though the abstract does not quantify wall-clock or token-cost savings.

p1_watchlist.title: Temporal Tactile Encoding and Compliance for Intent-Aware Robot-to-Human Bimanual Handover
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal VLA / tactile control
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work coupling a VLA model with temporal tactile encoding, proprioception, and a compliance controller for intent-aware bimanual handover. Human-subject evaluation shows complementary gains over visual-only and tactile-without-compliance baselines, but no measured inference latency or compute reduction is reported, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Testing Interchangeability in LLM Agent Teams
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent communication / coordination cost
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that swapping role-matched agents can preserve task score while increasing communication per unit progress by 16-63%, with larger penalties after longer team formation. This is useful systems characterization of hidden multi-agent coordination cost, but not an acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: One Word, Different Action: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Embodied Reasoning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-robot benchmark / language-conditioned action reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a real-robot benchmark that separates decision invariance from decision sensitivity under minimal instruction changes, multi-constraint reasoning, and real-RGB grounding. It exposes failures when multiple constraints must be composed into one executable action, making it useful protected Physical-AI coverage, but it is a benchmark rather than an inference-efficiency method.

p1_watchlist.title: Compact Neural Appearance Models for Efficient Gaussian Splatting
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / 3DGS / compact appearance representation / CUDA rendering
p1_watchlist.why: Performs an end-to-end comparison of spherical-harmonic and learned spherical appearance models inside one optimized differentiable CUDA rasterizer, and introduces compact per-primitive latent codes decoded by a tiny shared MLP. The representation directly targets per-primitive storage and memory traffic and includes rendering-performance evaluation, but the primary abstract does not expose a single quantitative speedup or memory-reduction figure, so it remains a protected high-value watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Proton Irradiation Characterization of an Open-Source ML Accelerator on a Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / Physical AI / FPGA accelerator reliability
p1_watchlist.why: System-level proton-irradiation study of an open-source Tensil neural-network accelerator on Zynq UltraScale+ running ResNet-20 inference, documenting availability loss and silent output corruption with implications for recovery and verifiable edge/space AI deployment. Important Physical-AI/edge accelerator reliability evidence, but not primarily an efficiency or acceleration contribution.

p1_watchlist.title: Cross-Domain Tracker Adaptation Without Target-Domain Labels via Vision-Language Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / vision-language agents / online perception adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: A VLM diagnostic agent inspects tracking failures and iteratively adjusts a detect-to-track pipeline without target-domain labels, recovering a substantial fraction of oracle adaptation performance. It is protected Physical-AI runtime adaptation evidence, but it does not primarily optimize inference compute or latency.

p1_watchlist.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / adaptive expert skipping
p1_watchlist.why: Training- and calibration-free token-adaptive expert skipping with offline spectral/prototype statistics and lightweight runtime table lookups. Strong quality at 50% expert skipping across multiple MoE LLMs, but current abstract lacks measured end-to-end systems speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: LIBERO-RECOVER: Beyond Task Success Towards Failure Recovery in Robotic Manipulation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / evaluation / failure recovery / robustness
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces 1,000+ real execution-failure scenarios on LIBERO across action retry, adaptation, object-state recovery, and environmental recovery, explicitly targeting VLA/WAM deployment robustness beyond nominal task success. It is a protected Physical-AI benchmark rather than a compute/serving acceleration paper, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: WeAgent-MMGenEdit: A Full-Stack Recipe for Multimodal Agentic Image Generation and Editing
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / video/image generation acceleration / agent runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Provides a full multimodal agent runtime with persistent evidence management plus post-training; a 30B-total/3B-active policy approaches a 1T-parameter agent. Relevant active-parameter/runtime lineage, but no direct latency or throughput ratio is given.

p1_watchlist.title: APEX-RBD: Mixed-Precision Exploration Framework for Hardware-Efficient Robot Dynamics Accelerator Design
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot accelerator / mixed precision / edge hardware
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-efficiency candidate. Automates mixed-precision design-space exploration for rigid-body-dynamics accelerators and reports up to 1.9x area reduction and 1.8x power savings across robotic platforms; valuable but focused on dynamics hardware rather than learned policy serving.

p1_watchlist.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / RAG / soft context compression / inference efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: DEX-Comp directly targets the inference overhead of long retrieved contexts by encoding documents into substantially shorter embedding sequences. Its two-stage recipe first distills correct uncompressed-RAG behavior, then uses RL only on cases the uncompressed system fails. This is highly relevant to serving efficiency, but the primary abstract emphasizes QA quality across retrieval depths and does not provide a measured latency/throughput or token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Large Language Models with At Most One Spike per Neuron
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / energy-efficient LLM / spiking inference
p1_watchlist.why: A fully time-to-first-spike LLM formulation is scaled to 1.5B parameters and reports extremely sparse event-driven activity with an energy estimate from spike counts. Because the paper explicitly notes this is a proxy under a cost model rather than measurement on neuromorphic hardware, it is preserved as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: MomentQuant: an even more minimalist interval method with linear time complexity for time series classification
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient inference / linear-time algorithms
p1_watchlist.why: MomentQuant replaces exact interval quantiles with Cornish-Fisher approximations, removes the sorting requirement and reduces inference complexity to linear time. The primary abstract reports the optimized Quant implementation is faster than the original and MomentQuant is faster again with only a tiny predictive-performance decrease, making it relevant to lightweight inference; however, no numeric deployment latency/throughput gain is given in the primary abstract, so it remains watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hierarchical agent runtime / decentralized robot control
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work that cleanly separates expensive LLM reasoning from fast local control: LLM inference is confined to round-level policy generation/refinement while a UCB bandit and policy-conditioned Double DQN execute tick-level actions. In the evaluated three-robot simulation, the complete configuration reached all 90 robot-round goals and achieved 42-tick median completion time, 25.0-39.1% lower than alternative configurations. The evidence is simulation-level task efficiency rather than measured inference latency/throughput, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / navigation memory / compact world representation / cost-aware planning
p1_watchlist.why: Learns a reusable Bellman-grounded cognitive map with compact coordinate encoding, enabling changing navigation goals without per-goal retraining. On grids up to 1,600 nodes it maintains full success with only 5% mean gap to Dijkstra, while memory growth is sublinear from 400 to 3,600 nodes. It is valuable protected evidence for compact embodied memory, but not a direct VLA/WAM inference accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: Deep Microcompression: Structured Pruning and Bit-packed Quantization for Microcontrollers
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / microcontroller inference / pruning / quantization
p1_watchlist.why: Hardware-aware MCU deployment pipeline combining structured pruning, QAT and fixed-length bit-packing; reports 55.8x weight compression and deployment on ATmega328P with 2KB SRAM. Valuable edge-AI systems signal but currently limited-model/MCU scope.

p1_watchlist.title: Efficient Multi-Timescale Event Representations for Feed-Forward Object Detection
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / event perception / feed-forward detection / neuromorphic efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Encodes multi-timescale temporal information directly in event representations and introduces a recursive approximation for efficient event-by-event updates, reducing reliance on recurrent temporal modeling while preserving detection performance. The primary abstract does not quantify latency, throughput, or energy gains, so it remains a protected Physical-AI watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: TROVE: Adaptive Agent Skill Orchestration via Trace-Grounded Route Validation and Editing
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive orchestration / compute avoidance
p1_watchlist.why: TROVE preserves valid workflow fragments and revises only execution steps invalidated by new runtime evidence, explicitly targeting wasted computation from stale plans and broad replanning. This is a useful agent-runtime adaptive-compute pattern, but the abstract does not provide a clean latency/token/cost reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: ARC-Loc: Leveraging Azimuthal Ray Convergence as a Geometric Cue for Direct Cross-View Localization
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / geometric localization / lightweight perception
p1_watchlist.why: ARC-Loc removes computationally heavy BEV transforms and external depth-foundation-model dependencies by direct ground-to-satellite geometric matching, reporting faster and more memory-efficient inference while keeping competitive localization accuracy. It is relevant to edge Physical-AI perception, but the abstract omits concrete latency/memory ratios.

p1_watchlist.title: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agent
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agentic RL / executable environments / training infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: Automates sandboxed executable-environment synthesis and topology-aware task generation, producing 139 environments and about 20K complex tasks. Qwen3/3.5 8B-32B models gain up to 11.9% on Claw benchmarks and 8.0% on tool-use benchmarks with reduced inference token cost, but the abstract does not quantify the cost reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: GreenPipe: Power Modeling for Containerized DNN Inference on Kubernetes Edge Nodes
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud heterogeneous AI systems / Kubernetes inference / online power modeling / energy-aware serving
p1_watchlist.why: 30d edge/heterogeneous replay recovered a current containerized inference systems paper absent from authority/watch. GreenPipe builds an automated external-meter profiling, regression-model training and validation pipeline for Raspberry-Pi/K3s DNN serving, covering precision/thread/local-vs-remote configurations and jointly reporting latency and energy. Retained as high-value watch because it is primarily measurement/modeling infrastructure rather than a new serving scheduler or accelerator mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal reasoning / CoT compression / KV pressure
p1_watchlist.why: Strong efficiency signal for multimodal reasoning: fewer than 900 training samples, up to 69.5% CoT-length reduction and up to 3.34x end-to-end inference speedup while preserving accuracy. Contribution is primarily algorithmic preference/compression rather than a serving-system design, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: One Diffusion Model, Two Roles: Guided Trajectory Planning and Safety-Critical Scenario Generation in Closed-Loop Simulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / autonomous driving / diffusion planning / closed-loop simulation
p1_watchlist.why: Uses one pretrained diffusion traffic model both as an ego planner and as a controllable safety-critical scenario generator, with training-free clean-sample guidance that avoids auxiliary networks. This is highly relevant to WAM/world-model and action-planning lineage, but the abstract emphasizes closed-loop quality and controllability rather than measured inference acceleration, so it remains protected watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Compact-Memory LLM Agents via Online Max-Member Clustering and Atom-Aware Packing
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory compression / long-horizon agents
p1_watchlist.why: Online clustered memory reaches 83% of full-context quality at 32% of token cost under a 4k budget and improves over streaming-cluster baselines; relevant to efficient long-horizon agents, though current evidence is token-budget efficiency rather than serving-system latency.

p1_watchlist.title: TourPhysics: Bringing Physics to World Models for Exploration and Manipulation from a Single Image
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / physics-grounded generation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected world-model work that couples deterministic simulation, geometric evidence, generator controls, and persistent appearance memory for online exploration and manipulation from a single image. It improves trajectory adherence and long-horizon revisit consistency over baselines, but does not report serving/runtime acceleration metrics, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Fast Gauss Sums via Flash Attention
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / efficient attention reuse
p1_watchlist.why: Maps arbitrary signed Gaussian kernel sums onto FlashAttention using small input augmentations, outperforming compiled PyTorch and PyKeOps for D>8 in fp16 while keeping linear memory scaling; useful kernel-reuse result, but it targets kernel methods rather than mainstream AI-inference workloads.

p1_watchlist.title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / expert cache / router adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Direct MoE inference memory/traffic optimization using jointly adapted temporal and spatio-temporal cache routers while preserving native Top-K; reports 4.6-53.3% expert-weight traffic reduction. Watch pending venue/adoption evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Reasoning Without Inference Cost: Latent Semantic Scaffolding for Robot VLA Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / zero-overhead reasoning / deployment efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI signal. Training-only semantic scaffolding aligns action-token representations to physical-reasoning rationale embeddings and drops the projection head at deployment, leaving the base VLA with zero added inference cost. Strong deployment-efficiency idea but primarily algorithmic and currently preprint-only, so high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: From Deep to Shallow: Unconstrained and Efficient Layer Merging Strategy
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / model compression / embedded inference
p1_watchlist.why: The method merges redundant layers without requiring an analytical merge rule and avoids the kernel-size growth that can erase practical speedups. The authors report inference speed-up measurements on real embedded platforms across architectures and datasets, making it relevant deployment evidence, but the abstract omits a clean numerical speedup ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: ReCAST: Restoration-aware Cascaded Stage-wise Training for Obfuscated SMS Risk Classification
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / distillation / deployable small models
p1_watchlist.why: ReCAST distills a large teacher de-obfuscation capability into a smaller deployable student under production-oriented latency and throughput constraints. It is relevant to compact production inference, but the abstract does not provide concrete speedup, memory, or cost numbers.

p1_watchlist.title: AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / autonomous ML engineering / production experimentation
p1_watchlist.why: NetEase production agent harness coordinates multi-day research-to-launch cycles with deterministic controllers retaining authority over execution, metric extraction, guardrails and persistent state. Important long-running agent/ML-infra lineage, though the abstract does not quantify wall-clock savings.

p1_watchlist.title: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / procedural memory / skill reuse
p1_watchlist.why: Converts interaction trajectories and evaluator feedback into a persistent versioned skill library while keeping the action-generation and grounding stack fixed. Across four OSWorld domains the evolving library improves post-warm-up evaluator scores by 5.7-18.6 points, providing useful evidence for reusable procedural memory without model updates.

p1_watchlist.title: Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / cloud-edge robotics / communication-aware world models
p1_watchlist.why: Couples control and wireless JEPA world models to predict robot and channel state and schedule uplink transmissions, explicitly targeting communication-efficient remote robotic control; currently validated in Gazebo-ROS-Sionna simulation rather than production deployment.

p1_watchlist.title: Communication-Efficient Personalized Federated Learning via Layer-Wise Multi-Threshold Random Sketching
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / federated learning / communication compression / low-bit sketching
p1_watchlist.why: Uses layer-specific multi-threshold random sketches for bidirectional personalized federated learning communication, improving the communication-accuracy tradeoff over one-bit compression baselines. The primary abstract does not report an exact byte, bandwidth, latency, or round reduction, so it is retained as a high-value systems watch rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: CPR-IE:A Compression-Prediction-Resource Intelligence Efficiency Metric
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficiency metric / deployment evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: CPR-IE proposes a deployment-oriented efficiency ordering that jointly accounts for compression, predictive quality and resource burden, with unit-invariant aggregation. It is useful as an evaluation lens for Efficient-ML comparisons, but it is a metric/protocol rather than an optimization technique.

p1_watchlist.title: Linguistic Trajectory Encoding for Efficient Long-Horizon Spatial Memory in Embodied Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / embodied agent memory / long-horizon spatial compression
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI memory-efficiency watch. LTE compresses per-object motion histories using language plus sparse spatial/visual anchors, adapting representation to motion complexity. The paper reports 8.7x-26.1x trajectory compression with sub-second queries over 24-hour video and substantial retrieval gains. Valuable for embodied long-context/memory census, though it is a memory representation rather than a full VLA/WAM serving runtime.

p1_watchlist.title: HaptiNet: Networked Haptic Robots Enable Physical Co-presence in Geographically-Unconstrained Rehabilitation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / distributed robotics / network delay compensation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI infrastructure: networked haptic robots use an imitation-learning delay compensator to preserve force-mediated interaction over geographically distributed links. Validation spans 284 healthy participants, 111 patients, and three intercity links totaling about 4,000 km. The work demonstrates robust distributed physical interaction but does not report a compute/serving speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: ProtLingo: Efficient Protein Language Modeling via Conditional Memory and Expert Routing
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / conditional memory / efficient language models
p1_watchlist.why: Combines conditional local memory with sparse expert routing in a protein language model and activates only a subset of expert parameters. Interesting efficiency mechanism, but primary evidence focuses on parameter/task efficiency rather than end-to-end systems latency or throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Diffusion Language Models for Mobile Edge Agentic AI: Foundations, Applications, and Challenges
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / diffusion language models / edge-cloud serving / mobile edge AI
p1_watchlist.why: 30d edge/agent replay recovered a systems-oriented survey absent from the authority union. It connects DLM parallel refinement and quality-latency elasticity to edge constraints including memory, energy, bandwidth, split inference, communication-aware serving, long-context state, and multimodal grounding. High lineage value, but its primary contribution is survey/taxonomy rather than a new runtime mechanism, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Resilience Beyond Stationary Client Unavailability: Unlocking Efficient and Unbiased Federated Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / federated learning / dynamic availability
p1_watchlist.why: FedSWE targets heterogeneous non-stationary client availability with missed-computation compensation, stabilized global updates and implicit gossip mixing while remaining agnostic to the availability process. It adds only light memory/compute overhead and has linear-speedup theory in special cases, but the primary abstract gives no exact measured runtime/communication reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / prefix cache / quantization / reproducibility
p1_watchlist.why: Direct serving-path measurement showing prefix-cache state can materially change multi-turn agent trajectories, with divergence increasing from 36.2% at 16-bit to 75.0% at 4-bit across two engines. Important cache+quantization systems reliability signal, but it is primarily a measurement/reproducibility study and currently only submitted to IEEE Access, so keep as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Where to Look Matters: Learning Influential Views for VLM-based 3D Visual Grounding
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / active vision / view selection
p1_watchlist.why: Trains a lightweight query-conditioned selector to choose influential camera views before frozen-VLM comparative grounding, replacing fixed visibility heuristics. Relevant adaptive-perception lineage, though accuracy rather than compute is the reported endpoint.

p1_watchlist.title: Aplaud: Adaptive Personalized Low-Rank Decomposition for User-Specific LLM
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / parameter-efficient adaptation / personalized LLM serving
p1_watchlist.why: Aplaud separates a frozen shared low-rank basis from compact per-user corrections and reports better generalization plus inference efficiency than LoRA-style personalized baselines. Relevant scalable personalization lineage, though the abstract omits a concrete memory/latency ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: HiSfM: Disambiguating Structure-from-Motion via Scaffold-Anchored Hierarchical Reconstruction
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / 3D vision pipeline efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Hierarchical coarse-to-fine SfM builds a compact verified scaffold and then absorbs remaining images, improving robustness under repeated/symmetric structure while substantially reducing runtime versus prior methods. Official author code is available, but the primary abstract does not report an exact latency or speedup figure, so it is retained as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: PLUME: Parameter-Efficient Personalization of Large Language Models via Low-Rank User Modulation in Shared Subspaces
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / parameter-efficient adaptation / personalization
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a shared task subspace plus tiny per-user modulation matrices and rank-1 residuals, reducing per-user parameters by over 95% while matching or improving personalization baselines.

p1_watchlist.title: Sustainable Edge Vision via Empirically Calibrated DVFS: Eliminating Thermal Throttling on Passively Cooled Hardware
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / DVFS / thermal-aware inference
p1_watchlist.why: Real hardware edge-inference scheduler on passively cooled Raspberry Pi 5. Eliminates observed thermal throttling, improves frame rate by 6.8% versus temperature-only control and reduces energy/frame by 1.9%; scope is narrow, so high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: LookThere! Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / adaptive vision inference / edge-efficient perception
p1_watchlist.why: End-to-end learned selector/extractor achieves a new performance-compute Pareto frontier and can retain accuracy with as little as 0.2% of the input on sparse high-resolution tasks, generalizing across classification, segmentation and regression. Strong adaptive-compute signal, but primarily a vision algorithm rather than AI-infra/serving system, so keep as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Occamy-1.0: Open Pareto-frontier 35B Intelligence for Co-work
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems
p1_watchlist.why: Recovered by official OAI-PMH reconciliation after /new HTML fallback; direct/high-value Efficient ML or AI Infra signal.

p1_watchlist.title: Choosing the Right Language Mode at Inference Time for Multilingual Reliability
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / adaptive inference / compute routing
p1_watchlist.why: RAAI performs calibration-aware routing and uses a mid-layer risk index to gate sequential reasoning, allocating extra compute only when likely to help. It improves low-resource-language accuracy and calibration, but the abstract does not quantify compute saved.

p1_watchlist.title: Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation of Diffusion Transformers
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / model compression
p1_watchlist.why: SVDtrunc allocates low-rank compression across DiT blocks and retains near-full FLUX.dev quality at 68% of original parameter count while remaining competitive at 57%; strong deployment-efficiency signal but no direct measured latency/throughput result in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: SCAPES: Semantically Conditioned Autoregressive Prior for Environmental Sounds
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / lightweight generative models / single-GPU training
p1_watchlist.why: SCAPES uses a 36M-parameter latent continuous-normalizing-flow model with flow matching and reports training on a single consumer GPU with convergence after roughly twice the source-audio duration. It is useful evidence for lightweight generative modeling, but it is not yet a direct image/video serving accelerator and lacks an end-to-end baseline speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / runtime safety
p1_watchlist.why: Runtime search/admission operator for ReAct tool agents using deterministic shadow execution and structured constraint state; strong systems/agent-runtime evidence, but not primarily an inference-throughput paper.

p1_watchlist.title: $τ^τ$-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / serving-cost benchmark / agent construction
p1_watchlist.why: $τ^τ$-Bench makes serving cost and model choice part of end-to-end agent construction across 53 realistic tasks and evaluates deployed agents against held-out users. It is useful infrastructure evidence for cost-aware agent engineering, but is a benchmark rather than an acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Open-Set 3D Scene Graphs for Field Robotics: An Outdoor Case Study
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / scene graph memory / field robotics / open-set VLM mapping
p1_watchlist.why: Systematically evaluates semantic embeddings, graph navigation, region understanding and memory size of an open-set 3D scene graph across five outdoor robotic datasets, including repeated-traversal consistency. It is valuable evidence for persistent spatial memory and VLM-grounded world-state infrastructure, but it is a characterization study rather than a measured inference-acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: JLIR: A Julia-Native MLIR-Inspired Intermediate Representation with Automatic JACC Kernel Extraction
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / Julia IR / accelerator kernel extraction
p1_watchlist.why: Compiler-infrastructure contribution bringing MLIR-style extensible IR into Julia with automatic JACC accelerator-kernel extraction. Relevant to DSL/compiler route, but current primary evidence does not yet establish strong AI-workload performance impact.

p1_watchlist.title: Optimizer Memory Schedules for Outscaling the Overtraining Axis
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / optimizer efficiency / training compute
p1_watchlist.why: Systematically studies optimizer memory and training-horizon scaling from 51M to 253M parameters and 1x-256x overtraining. Muon and SOAP retain token-efficiency advantages while ADANA closes the gap at long horizons; useful training-efficiency lineage though the abstract lacks one clean wall-clock speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Training-Free Halving of Activated Experts in Fine-Grained Mixture-of-Experts Models
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / expert pruning / inference efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free method separates active expert count from probability-mass normalization, halving routed-expert compute on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with only 0.35 MMLU-point loss and replicating on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Strong algorithmic MoE-efficiency signal but lacks measured serving latency/throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Dynamic Adaptation of the LLM Context for Generating Routines with Coupled Semantics
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / dynamic context / sample-efficient search
p1_watchlist.why: A validation agent converts execution traces into structured diagnostics that dynamically adapt generation context, outperforming Reflexion and OpenEvolve at matched 300-600 evaluation budgets on most tested problems. This is useful sample-efficiency evidence for agentic code search, but not a direct serving accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: La Agente Óptima: Towards Agentic Self-Driving Laboratories
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / autonomous experimentation / conditional agent invocation
p1_watchlist.why: Separates LLM reasoning from persistent Bayesian-optimization campaigns: repetitive closed-loop optimization proceeds without repeatedly invoking the agent, and control returns to the LLM only when interpretation or campaign revision is needed. This conditional-invocation pattern is relevant to Physical-AI runtime design, but no clean inference-speedup metric is given in the abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for Post-Deployment Physical AI
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / on-device adaptation / post-deployment runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI deployment signal. CFAM performs autonomous gradient-free on-device post-deployment updates across five embodiments and reports 2.5x fewer prior-training trajectories plus +13.9pp action success after near-OOD field updates. Systems/deployment relevance is real, but the contribution remains model/learning-framework heavy and lacks a strong systems venue, so high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge perception / human-robot interaction
p1_watchlist.why: SocioGesture uses a compact confidence-aware skeleton representation and lightweight dual-stream model for low-latency onboard social-gesture recognition, and runs in real time on a robot-mounted edge device with deployment-time adaptation. It is useful protected Physical-AI runtime evidence, but the abstract lacks concrete latency/throughput numbers.

p1_watchlist.title: LentEx: Generalizable Latent Entity Extraction via Synthetic Data and Instruction-Tuned LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration
p1_watchlist.why: LentEx explicitly fine-tunes smaller efficient LLMs for latent-entity extraction using synthetic supervision; useful compact-RAG preprocessing lineage but systems gains are secondary.

p1_watchlist.title: Toward Sustainable Distributed LLM Inference: A Systems Synthesis and Research Agenda for an Energy-, Carbon-, and Cache-Aware llm-d Control Plane
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / distributed inference / cache-aware scheduling / sustainable systems
p1_watchlist.why: Systems synthesis connecting model/phase/cache/hardware/replica/region/time decisions for distributed LLM inference and proposing an energy-, carbon-, and cache-aware llm-d control plane with SLO-satisfied goodput-per-joule and per-CO2e evaluation. It explicitly states that its contribution is synthesis rather than new benchmark results, so it is retained as a high-value systems agenda watch rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: STyMo: Fast and Controllable Few-Shot Motion Style Transfer
p1_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / motion generation / rapid adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Few-shot motion style transfer trains from only seconds of paired data in one to two minutes by decomposing static posture and temporal dynamics, enabling an iterative authoring loop with runtime-controllable style factors. Clear adaptation-time efficiency, though outside core LLM serving.

p1_watchlist.title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back in Low-Precision Temporal Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / recurrent-state memory / inference reliability
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that deterministic 4-bit recurrent-state storage can catastrophically amplify error over time, and that error-feedback/residual-memory write-back can recover accuracy without retraining. The result is domain-specific but exposes a general systems interface issue for low-precision stateful inference.

p1_watchlist.title: Towards Understanding Pause Token Fine-Tuning Dynamics: A Mode Retention Perspective
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems
p1_watchlist.why: Pause-token study reports roughly 4x less overwrite at matched adaptation and explores masked boundary pauses as compressed latent reasoning state; useful efficient-reasoning/training-dynamics lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: Performance Study of Serverless Workloads in Confidential Virtual Machines
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / confidential serverless / memory and startup overhead
p1_watchlist.why: This empirical systems study characterizes warm/cold-start and memory-efficiency overheads of serverless workloads inside confidential VMs, identifying page-deduplication/reclaimability and VMEXIT effects and practical mitigation directions. It is high-value cloud-systems characterization, but not a new broadly faster runtime with headline speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: GRACE: Graph-Grounded Reflective Agent Copilot Engine for Expert-in-the-Loop Knowledge Expansion
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / cost-aware verification / RAG agents
p1_watchlist.why: GRACE uses a Return-on-Attention objective to defer uncertain claims to expert or agent review only when priority-weighted uncertainty justifies verification cost. This is relevant adaptive-compute evidence for agentic RAG, but lacks a clean latency or dollar-cost reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: ICM-Bench: Person-Level Identity Reasoning in Multimodal Agents with Long-Term Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / long-term memory / benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: ICM-Bench isolates identity-centric long-term memory over 839 synthetic clips and 1,217 questions and compares caption-memory, memory-augmented agents and graph retrieval. It is a useful memory-system evaluation node, but primarily a benchmark rather than an efficiency method.

p1_watchlist.title: Accelerating Atom Simulations with Variable-Block Sparse Matrix Library
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / distributed sparse linear algebra / scientific AI infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: VBCSR preserves variable-size atomic blocks and groups equal-shape blocks for optimized dense-kernel dispatch, with a unified CSR/BSR/VBCSR interface and a demonstration above one million atoms. The abstract states it outperforms tested Python-accessible references but does not expose a quantified end-to-end speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: FAVE: Foveated Adaptive Visual Encoding for Efficient Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / visual-token efficiency / adaptive encoding
p1_watchlist.why: Strong MLLM efficiency signal: variable-resolution foveated encoding, 12.7x lower FLOPs in a controlled small-object setting and 3.3x controlled TTFT speedup when integrated with FastVLM. Current contribution is primarily model/encoding design rather than a full serving-system paper, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: LLM-Aided Design for Manufacturing: A Multi-Agent System for Intent-Preserving Redesign of CAD for Improved Manufacturability
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / industrial agents / tool-using verification
p1_watchlist.why: A multimodal-LLM reviewer and CAD-modifier agent iteratively propose, compile, visually verify and revise manufacturing-oriented CAD edits. It is useful lineage for tool-using industrial Physical-AI agents, but the contribution is task robustness rather than inference efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: SharedSAE: One Feature Dictionary Across Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / interpretability infrastructure / shared representation
p1_watchlist.why: SharedSAE replaces separate per-model sparse-autoencoder dictionaries with one shared dictionary plus model-specific encoder-decoder pairs; it retains 96.6% of dedicated-SAE explained variance and allows efficient adaptation of new models while reusing labels. This materially reduces duplicated interpretability infrastructure, though it is not inference-serving acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: TokenMatch: 3D Mesh Correspondence Transformer with Curvature-Guided Tokenisation
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / 3D tokenization / feed-forward inference
p1_watchlist.why: TokenMatch replaces costly generative functional-map inference with a feed-forward transformer using curvature-guided tokenization and cross-attention, motivated explicitly by inference cost and generalization. Relevant token-efficiency lineage, but the abstract lacks a quantified speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Temporal Self-Distillation: Learning Visual State Tracking in Videos Without Supervision
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / video understanding / self-distillation
p1_watchlist.why: S3T uses denser temporal views as an internal teacher for a sparse-view student with shared weights, requiring no labels, separate teacher, or reward signal and adding no inference cost. It improves LLaVA-OneVision video-state tracking, though the efficiency gain is primarily training/data-side rather than measured serving speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / online 3D reconstruction / lightweight pose queries
p1_watchlist.why: Scal3R keeps the reconstruction backbone frozen and adds lightweight multi-reference pose-query tokens amounting to about 1% of parameters to stabilize long-video online 3D reconstruction. It is a strong lightweight Physical-AI perception idea, but the abstract does not provide a clean wall-clock or memory reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / local inference / distillation
p1_watchlist.why: Fresh efficiency-adjacent work that compiles recurring natural-language functions into reusable compact local neural functions, avoiding repeated remote LLM calls and their latency/cost/provider dependency. Strong deployment motivation but no broad end-to-end systems benchmark yet, so retain as P1 watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / representation learning / action-oriented structure
p1_watchlist.why: Architecture-flexible structural supervision preserves geometry, affordance, and goal information in intermediate features across VLA, direct-action WAM, and inverse-dynamics WAM. On LIBERO-Plus the three variants reach 79.6%, 72.6%, and 87.8%, and on RoboCasa 61.4%, 83.6%, and 82.3%; important protected Physical-AI work but not a measured inference-speed method.

p1_watchlist.title: Iris: Climbing to the Search Frontier
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / search agents / context management
p1_watchlist.why: Iris trains search agents with SFT-RL climbing and explicitly returns the hardest solved and most efficient rollouts to the next supervised stage. The evaluation isolates inference-time context management because it matters more than many reported system differences, making this strong agent-runtime lineage even though the abstract does not give a clean latency or token-reduction ratio.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Retrieval: Progressive Latent Memory Evolution for Streaming Video Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / bounded latent memory
p1_watchlist.why: LatentStream targets continuous causal video understanding under a fixed memory budget, using hierarchical streaming memory and compact fixed-length evolving latent tokens. It reports SOTA quality but no measured latency/throughput/system speedup in the primary abstract, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / terminal agents / RL environment infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: Off-policy environment evolution incrementally raises difficulty and schedules evolved tasks generation by generation, avoiding sole reliance on on-policy rollout synthesis. Long-horizon RL improves Qwen3.6-27B and 35B-A3B by 14.4 and 18.0 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1; relevant agent-training infrastructure, though not an inference-efficiency result.

p1_watchlist.title: Adaptive Vision-Language Grasping via Composable Foundation Priors and Generalizable Grasp Synthesis
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / modular foundation-model priors / grasp runtime
p1_watchlist.why: AdaRoboVLG decouples a reusable physically grounded grasp base policy from task-dependent foundation-model priors, allowing new spatial/cognitive/temporal priors to be composed without retraining the underlying grasp policy. Protected Physical-AI modular-runtime lineage; abstract claims efficient learning but lacks measured inference savings.

p1_watchlist.title: TAP-Path: Task-Adaptive Structural and Token Pruning for Efficient and Trustworthy Pathology Foundation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / multimodal models / efficient inference
p1_watchlist.why: Combines transformer-block removal and adaptive patch-token pruning, reducing encoder parameters by about 25% and analytical compute by 35.2% while preserving or improving pathology accuracy. Strong compression signal but currently domain-specific and without measured systems latency.

p1_watchlist.title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / autonomous driving / non-autoregressive action
p1_watchlist.why: LaPla uses concurrent action queries in one forward pass and a frozen VQ-VAE decoder to bypass time-consuming autoregressive action generation. Closed-loop AlpaSim results report substantially reduced inference latency and strong success gains, but the abstract lacks a concrete latency/speedup number, so retain as protected Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Sparse auto-regressive modeling for scene generation from multi-view images

p1_watchlist.why: SPAR3S learns a compact voxel-aligned 3D latent space in which only occupied voxels are represented, then jointly predicts sparse occupancy and latent tokens with a masked autoregressive transformer. The sparse representation directly targets dense-volumetric compute cost and uses differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting supervision, but the primary abstract reports no exact runtime or memory reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: OctWorld: Long-Range World-Consistent Video Generation with Octree-Based 3D Mapping

p1_watchlist.why: OctWorld adds a persistent OctMap memory using TSDF fusion in a dynamic sparse octree to stabilize long-range autoregressive video world generation under revisits. The sparse adaptive 3D memory is structurally relevant to efficient world-model generation, but the primary abstract does not report a concrete latency, throughput, or memory reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: FWBC-VLA: Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation

Real-world wiping and door-opening experiments demonstrate deployment relevance, but the current abstract does not provide comparative serving latency, throughput, memory, or compute-speedup numbers, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation

Accepted at EMNLP 2026 Main, but watermarking is adjacent rather than a core serving primitive, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: SimSkill: A Lifelong Learning AI Agent for Autonomous Mastery of Traffic Simulation

p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-time robot control / model-based runtime

p1_watchlist.title: Bringing dApps to OCUDU: An E3 Controller for Real-Time Open RAN Intelligence

p1_watchlist.title: Who Speaks for the Pruned? Visual Token Pruning as Coverage Optimization

p1_watchlist.why: CoverPruner formulates training-free visual-token pruning as representational coverage maximization and reports the best average accuracy across multiple VLMs and compression rates, especially under aggressive pruning. p1_watchlist.title: RACE-AIMC: Selective Inference for Heterogeneous Analog In-Memory Accelerators at the Edge

p1_watchlist.title: Sensing Which Modality Matters: Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust VLA Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal robustness / zero-overhead inference / sensor fusion
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a VLA robustness method whose evidence-gated regularization adds zero inference-time overhead and substantially improves real-robot robustness under sensor corruption and distractors. Because the core contribution is algorithmic robustness rather than measured serving acceleration or systems throughput, it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Solving the Needle-in-a-Haystack Problem in Mammography Vision-Language Model with Differentiable Subset Sampling

p1_watchlist.why: TopKSigLIP sparsely samples high-resolution mammography patches instead of downscaling full images, useful multimodal sparse-token/patch-selection lineage despite medical scope.

p1_watchlist.title: Compute-in-Memory Attention: A Time-Domain Analog Softmax Circuit with RC-Tunable Temperature

p1_watchlist.why: Relevant attention-accelerator circuit that eliminates an intermediate ADC path by applying tunable time-domain analog softmax directly to CIM score voltages. Post-layout 22-nm simulations report 242.97 ns, 13.44 mW and 25.5 pJ/output element for 128-way softmax, with hardware-aware Transformer loss within 2.5% of ideal. Simulation-only evidence keeps it watchlist-high rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: GPU-Accelerated Astrodynamics World Models for Spacecraft Rendezvous and Proximity Operations
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / GPU simulation
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces an open-source JAX GPU-parallel spacecraft environment and a flow-matching world model for autonomous rendezvous, with improved sample efficiency and docking success. It is a useful Physical-AI world-model/runtime signal, but not yet a serving or deployment-efficiency paper.

p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / sparse decoding / visual token retrieval
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free single-pass LVLM decoding combines semantics-directed visual-token sparsification with on-demand semantic-space visual retrieval, explicitly avoiding multi-round decoding overhead while retaining long-context hallucination suppression. p1_watchlist.title: Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improves data efficiency

It keeps physically packed low-bit cache formats fixed and distills floating-cache behavior into low-rank Q/K/V projection updates, recovering substantial held-out perplexity gaps across multiple models/quantizers while showing that perplexity recovery does not necessarily recover long-context retrieval. Useful evidence for quantized-KV deployment tradeoffs, but currently narrower and more adaptation-centric than a new serving runtime mechanism.
