tracking_records.title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking
tracking_records.topic: sparsity/pruning / efficient attention / long-context / Triton kernel
tracking_records.why: SAS learns context ranking end-to-end under a fixed sparse-attention budget instead of distilling dense attention scores, and includes a memory-efficient Triton kernel integrated into FlashAttention-style computation for long-sequence training. It outperforms trainable sparse-attention baselines across reasoning, long-context and agentic tasks, especially at tight budgets.

tracking_records.title: Rethinking Heterogeneous System Disaggregation for Subquadratic Attention
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / efficient attention / heterogeneous disaggregation / energy-efficient inference
tracking_records.why: SQD revisits heterogeneous disaggregation specifically for subquadratic-attention LLMs, mapping attention/state-heavy and dense compute phases to heterogeneous resources rather than assuming standard quadratic-attention serving. It reports substantial tokens-per-joule gains across modern hybrid/subquadratic models and tighter latency plus higher throughput in projected Rubin+LPX systems.

tracking_records.title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / diffusion / action decoding
tracking_records.why: Unified diffusion VLA/WAM with goal/action/future-state composition; optimized block-parallel action decoding reports up to 29.2x model-side speedup.

tracking_records.title: Attention Quantization for Tabular Foundation Models
tracking_records.topic: quantization / efficient attention / GPU kernels
tracking_records.why: FP8 Q/K/V attention quantization with explicit FP8 matmul and Triton kernel; up to 1.7x speedup without relevant accuracy loss on evaluated tabular foundation models.

tracking_records.title: SeqMoE: Toward Full-Load Performance via Predictive and Graph-Compatible MoE Offloading
tracking_records.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / LLM serving / offloading
tracking_records.why: Predictive sequence-model expert activation, deadline-aware prefetch, forecast-driven cache and graph-compatible runtime; 45% residency reaches 80.22% of full-load performance.

tracking_records.title: 4D Parallelism Unlocks Exascale Bayesian Neural Networks for High-Fidelity Atmospheric Modeling
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / heterogeneous AI systems
tracking_records.why: BEAST introduces orthogonal 4D parallelization with domain-tensor parallelism and uncertainty parallelism; reports 3.96 EFLOP/s on 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs for a 2.4B-parameter configuration.

tracking_records.title: RoofLang: Enabling AI-Driven Architecting of LLM Inference Systems
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / system architecture DSL / AI-driven design-space exploration
tracking_records.why: RoofLang is a DSL and optimization framework for representing and searching LLM inference-system architectures, turning serving design into an executable architecture search problem. The paper reports large decode-throughput opportunity for DeepSeek V4-series designs and persistent optimizer agents finding B300 architectures with sizeable throughput/interactivity improvements.

tracking_records.title: HeatCache: Thermal-aware Energy-efficient LLM Inference Scheduling for Chassis-level Liquid Cooling in Sustainable Edge Server Rooms
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / edge inference / thermal-aware scheduling / energy efficiency
tracking_records.why: HeatCache integrates thermal state into LLM scheduling for liquid-cooled edge-server rooms and is evaluated in a vLLM-based serving stack. It reports up to 18.0% lower compute energy, 81.7% lower thermal-throttle exposure and sub-0.9% SLO violations at elevated coolant temperatures.

tracking_records.title: HoliBench: A Cross-Platform Benchmarking and Deployment Toolkit for Foundation Models in CPS-IoT Applications
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / benchmarking / deployment
tracking_records.why: Open-source cross-platform deployment toolkit jointly measuring accuracy, latency and energy across devices, modalities, inference engines and quantization levels.

tracking_records.title: OneLA: Scaling Linear-Attention Decoding to Large Beams in Generative Recommendation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / efficient attention / GPU kernels / generative recommendation
tracking_records.why: Linear-attention serving framework for large-beam decoding that shares prompt-derived recurrent state, stores compact append-only divergent transitions and uses a fused GPU kernel; reports 1.54-2.46x end-to-end decode speedups.

tracking_records.title: ForgeMegakernel: A General Framework for Efficient Auto-Regressive Model Decode Megakernels
tracking_records.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / LLM serving / decode megakernel generation
tracking_records.why: ForgeMegakernel uses coding agents plus a mid-state correctness oracle to generate per-model decode megakernels with fine-grained per-SM instruction streams, dependency counters and shared-memory buffer pooling. Across 14 decoding operations and eight model families it reports 1.21x geometric-mean speedup over SGLang 0.5.18 and 1.54x over a megakernel compiler, with all tested kernels faster inside SGLang at comparable accuracy.

tracking_records.title: Unleashing the Power of Equality Saturation for Tensor Program Superoptimization
tracking_records.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / efficient attention
tracking_records.why: EqiForge unifies high-level tensor expressions and tiled computations in one IR and uses equality saturation plus early compaction to search fused implementations, including FlashAttention-style kernels.

tracking_records.title: Argus: Orchestrating Cross-Layer GPU Performance Measurements around Semantic Regions
tracking_records.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / AI infra / performance tooling
tracking_records.why: Region-centric measurement planner/runtime joining compiler, hardware and system evidence; improves persistent-kernel optimization and multi-GPU PGO.

tracking_records.title: Vortex: Bridging Extreme Compression and Efficient LLM Inference
tracking_records.topic: quantization / sparsity / LLM accelerator / compressed inference
tracking_records.why: Vortex co-designs extreme vector quantization and contextual sparsity with an accelerator architecture that remains compatible with systolic-array execution. The paper reports 8.03-23.7x speedup and 5.68-12.5x energy reduction over compared state-of-the-art accelerators, making it a direct algorithm-architecture Efficient ML contribution.

tracking_records.title: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Management and Serving for Robot Factories
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multi-robot multi-model edge serving / SLO-aware multi-GPU runtime
tracking_records.why: Robion is a direct VLA serving and management system for multi-robot, multi-model requests on multi-GPU edge servers. It co-schedules VLM and action-diffusion stages with GPU stream/SM controls, placement and SLO-aware batching; the paper reports 6.7x higher supported robot load than vLLM-Omni for individual models at 98% SLO attainment and up to 64 robots for eight models on four GPUs.

tracking_records.title: AccelForge: Comprehensive Modeling and Co-Design Framework for AI Accelerators
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / accelerator modeling and co-design
tracking_records.why: AccelForge unifies device, circuit, architecture, workload, and mapping models, with composable models and fast mappers that evaluate designs orders of magnitude faster in computer and human time than prior workflows.

tracking_records.title: Building py-kvcache: A Performance Characterization of External KV Caching for vLLM with NVMe SSDs
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / KV cache / NVMe offload
tracking_records.why: Scheduler-aware asynchronous NVMe KV preloading overlaps disk reads with waiting/compute. At 80k tokens disk loading is 2.0x faster than LMCache; with GPU/CPU/disk tiers enabled it is 1.23x faster and within about 4% of native vLLM KV Offload.

tracking_records.title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / efficient reasoning / output-token reduction
tracking_records.why: Selects a task-aware low-rank post-training subspace that minimizes output-token cost under a utility constraint while updating only 0.24-0.28% of parameters. Continuation length falls by up to 39.84% on Pythia-2.8B and 14.87-17.58% on Qwen2.5-3B without material change in the internal preference diagnostic.

tracking_records.title: Structured Transforms for Low-Overhead Quantization of Language Models
tracking_records.topic: quantization / low-overhead LLM compression
tracking_records.why: Replacing dense random orthogonal transforms with sign-randomized DCT reduces each quantization iteration from O(N^2) to O(N log N), removes multi-restart k-means initialization, and shows favorable wall-clock scaling while producing native-2-bit-suited factors.

tracking_records.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent runtime harness
tracking_records.why: Cross-instance failure diagnosis accelerates self-evolving runtime-harness training. The paper reports up to 1.84x harness-training speedup while improving resulting reasoning accuracy by 18.56%.

tracking_records.title: A Training-Free, Alignment-Free Approach to Corporate Intelligence: Application to SEC Filings
tracking_records.topic: Efficient ML / AI Infra
tracking_records.why: Training-free sparse deterministic representations avoid embedding-model training/alignment and support sub-second document comparison on ordinary CPUs, providing concrete low-cost foundation-model alternative evidence.

tracking_records.title: OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs
tracking_records.topic: KV cache/long-context / quantization / multimodal serving
tracking_records.why: Training-free modality-aware KV quantization handles temporal key drift and heterogeneous value geometry in audio-video-text caches. Enables 2-bit KV caches on Qwen2.5-Omni/Qwen3-Omni and provides a fused Triton decode kernel that never materializes dense FP16 KV.

tracking_records.title: Entwine: Coordinating Tiled Computation and Fine-Grained Communication across GPUs
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / GPU communication overlap / tensor parallelism
tracking_records.why: Coordinates tile computation order, fine-grained SM communication, and SM allocation. Across tensor-parallel LLM workloads it achieves 1.232x geomean speedup, up to 1.433x, over cuBLAS+NCCL and beats state-of-the-art overlap baselines by 3.1-9.8% geomean.

tracking_records.title: Memory as Plans: World-Action Modeling with Memory-Grounded Planning
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / memory and long-horizon runtime
tracking_records.why: MaP-WAM converts long multimodal episodic memory into compact plans, keeps executor context length fixed, and enables KV caching in planning and execution. It reaches 83.3% RMBench and 78.0% real-robot success while maintaining approximately constant executor inference latency as history grows.

tracking_records.title: Characterizing Job Power Elasticity for Power-Flexible AI Training
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / datacenter power scheduling
tracking_records.why: A systematic characterization of LLM-training power elasticity over 131 H200 runs plus validation and H100 matches. PFI-aware allocation under a 30% power reduction recovers about 1.5k tokens/s per job, 63% of the gap between equal allocation and an oracle.

tracking_records.title: Calibration-Aware Uncertainty Cascades for Efficient Heterogeneous Model Collaboration
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / adaptive model routing
tracking_records.why: Post-hoc calibrated confidence creates a common reliability scale across heterogeneous models. Across six language benchmarks it avoids about 47% of strong-model calls while improving average accuracy, and reduces measured GFLOPs by up to 57% on image classification.

tracking_records.title: PATTON: Enabling Commodity PIM for Production LLM Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / KV cache / PIM accelerator runtime
tracking_records.why: Integrates production KV lifecycle management with commodity PIM using hierarchical granule allocation and a Commit Zone for efficient Value writes. Reports 1.95x average speedup and 4.83x energy efficiency over evaluated baselines without PIM processing-unit changes.

tracking_records.title: VikingRAG: Accurate and Token-efficient Retrieval-augmented Generation over Structured Documents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / token-efficient RAG serving
tracking_records.why: Directory-aware semantic retrieval, trace reuse, and adaptive escalation cut token use to 11.6%-51.9% of prior systems, and to 5.1%-32.5% with experience-edge reuse and escalation, while retaining competitive accuracy.

tracking_records.title: Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / sandbox memory / runtime compression
tracking_records.why: AgentZip exploits template-relative and cross-sandbox redundancy and aligns compression with LLM waiting periods. It cuts sandbox-owned memory by up to 8.7x versus 2.1x for Linux; restore prefetching and execution-aware scheduling reduce aggressive-compression slowdown from as high as 3.1x to 1.40x while retaining nearly all memory savings.

tracking_records.title: A Voice-Interactive Multi-Agent System for Smart Operating Rooms: Architecture Design and Key Technologies
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / agent systems / KV cache / streaming execution
tracking_records.why: Implements Qwen3-27B with llama.cpp/SGLang and combines byte-level KV-prefix warming, streaming partial-JSON parsing with early parallel execution, and progressive skill-prompt disclosure. Prefix reuse reduces recomputation from about 500 ms to tens of milliseconds and streaming execution cuts end-to-end latency by about 30%. Domain deployment is surgical, but the runtime techniques are directly reusable LLM-serving mechanisms.

tracking_records.title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG / context compression
tracking_records.why: Mines historical generator attention into reusable document-keyed evidence views instead of running an online compressor per query. Cuts compression overhead by 5.3-15.6x, adds under 40 ms latency, and improves generation quality by 1.0-5.8 points.

tracking_records.title: FlexComp: One Model for Every Ratio in Context Compression
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / context compression / adaptive inference
tracking_records.why: Any-ratio context compressor chooses memory budget per input via cascade routing or a lightweight predictor. tracking_records.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration
tracking_records.topic: mixed-precision attention kernel / long-context inference
tracking_records.why: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. Existing methods either use a uniform low-precision path or select token interactions, leaving spatial precision routing over hardware-aligned score tiles outside fused dense attention. We introduce TileMix, a tile-centric precision-routing kernel that makes numerical precision an executable spatial decision over score-tile groups within fused dense attention. TileMix partitions the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles, packs routing decisions into compact bitmasks, and dispatches each tile group through FP16 or INT8 score computation while both paths update a shared online-softmax state. Scalable precision grouping lets each routing bit govern multiple adjacent key tiles, preserving hardware-aligned compute tiles and compact metadata at long contexts. By routing all legal tile groups, TileMix preserves dense token connectivity, requires no training, and supports grouped-query attention, variable-length batches, and INT8 key/value caches. Across LongEval, LV-Eval, and A100 prefill benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna, TileMix recovers long-context quality lost under uniform INT8 and improves prefill throughput over FP16, yielding a controllable accuracy-efficiency frontier across model families. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.

Reallocating containers is too heavyweight to utilize such fine-grained opportunities under SLA constraints, and operator-level scheduling requires reasoning about dependencies, memory safety, and cluster-wide execution dynamics in real time. In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. tracking_records.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
tracking_records.topic: MoE expert-parallel load balancing / serving
tracking_records.why: In expert-parallel (EP) MoE serving, every layer synchronizes at the slowest GPU. Dispatchers balance token counts (EPLB, LPLB, UltraEP) or activated-expert counts (METRO), assuming expert time is linear in one. Measurements on two datacenter GPU generations show it is neither: below $n^* \approx 156$--$168$ tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates---cost attaches to $activated replicas$, not tokens; above it, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile $M$-tiles, so $splitting$ an expert adds padded compute. A max-affine profile $t=\max(a+bG,\,c+βN)$ captures both regimes. Realistic decode batches hold hot experts in the linear regime and cold in the flat $simultaneously$; recorded batches show proxy dispatches differ by $1.4$--$1.6\times$ in modeled block time (p95 up to $1.7\times$), and $which$ proxy wins flips with the regime. We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. Anchored by an 8-GPU Testbed A microbenchmark, TEMPO stays within $1\%$ of the best fixed baseline everywhere and wins by up to $15.5\%$ where regimes mix. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

tracking_records.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
tracking_records.topic: sparse video attention / DiT inference
tracking_records.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

tracking_records.why: Diffusion models have achieved dominant performance in visual generation but suffer from substantial inference overhead. While cache-based acceleration has emerged as a promising solution, existing policies rely on local similarity heuristics, which we identify as being significantly misaligned with final generation quality. This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

tracking_records.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding
tracking_records.topic: MoE architecture / small-batch decoding
tracking_records.why: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have been widely adopted in real-time interactive applications such as coding assistants, real-time audio-video interaction systems. To meet the extremely low response latency requirements of these scenarios, practitioners commonly employ small-batch decoding, under which MoE inference becomes memory-bound and is severely bottlenecked by expert weight loading. However, this bottleneck has received limited attention, and existing solutions such as post-training weight compression or fine-grained expert design during pre-training either degrade model accuracy or introduce additional computation and communication overhead. To tackle this issue, we propose DeaMoE, a decoding-efficient MoE architecture, in which the experts are grouped into several departments, and the experts belonging to the same department share most parameters since they come from the same professional field, and additionally each expert contains a few private parameters to reflect its uniqueness. Moreover, we design customized two-stage routing strategy for DeaMoE to avoid redundant loading, under which DeaMoE greatly improves the efficiency during LLM decoding. Compared with vanilla MoE, DeaMoE reduces per-step loaded weights by up to 50.9% and achieves up to 1.33 end-to-end TPOT speedup for the pre-trained 7B model on A40, and up to 2.00x and 1.97x peak speedup for DeepSeek-V3 on A40 and H100 in microbenchmarks.

tracking_records.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
tracking_records.topic: MoE serving / high-bandwidth flash architecture
tracking_records.why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

tracking_records.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / edge agents / on-device SLM / function calling

Important protected edge-Physical-AI evidence, but no exact latency or memory numbers are reported in the abstract.

tracking_records.title: OmniEye: Efficient Multimodal Forensic Video Intelligence for Law-Enforcement Body-Worn Cameras
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge deployment / quantization
tracking_records.why: OmniEye processes 30-second audiovisual windows with a multimodal foundation model, stores structured outputs in SQLite/BM25, and re-perceives only retrieved candidate windows for grounded questioning. The complete system is reported to run on a single 16 GB GPU using a 4-bit quantization-aware-trained model, giving useful deployment evidence for retrieval-gated multimodal serving, but without a direct speedup baseline.

tracking_records.title: Do Agents Know When They Succeed? Calibrating Agent Confidence from Internal Representations
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / runtime reliability / confidence monitoring
tracking_records.why: Uses residual-stream trajectory dynamics and action-representation probes to predict eventual agent success across Bash, SQL, and Python tasks and three model families. It reports a zero-overhead reliability monitor requiring neither prompt changes nor multi-sample rollouts; highly relevant to low-cost agent runtime control, but the abstract does not quantify end-to-end serving savings.

tracking_records.title: Efficient Leakage-Free Neural Architecture Search under Leave-One-Subject-Out Evaluation
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / neural architecture search / model compression
tracking_records.why: Block-based leakage-free NAS avoids fully nested O(N^2) search and reduces model parameters by up to 99.2% on BioVid while slightly improving mean accuracy. Good resource-efficiency evidence, but currently narrow in task/domain and lacks standardized GPU-hour reduction.

tracking_records.title: QPS-ToR: A Parallel Iterative Switching Algorithm for Reconfigurable Optical Datacenter Switching
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / datacenter networking / optical switching / low-complexity scheduling

The system result is strong, but the current paper is workload-agnostic rather than AI-specific, so it is retained as high-value AI-infrastructure networking evidence instead of canonical strong.

tracking_records.title: VANTAGE-Bench: Evaluating the Infrastructure AI Gap in Vision-Language Models
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / fixed-camera infrastructure VLM benchmark
tracking_records.why: Benchmarks 17 VLMs across logistics, transportation and smart-space infrastructure video, including long-horizon tracking and spatio-temporal tasks. tracking_records.title: Encrypt What Matters: When Selective Homomorphic Inference Is Efficient
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / privacy-preserving inference / selective FHE
tracking_records.why: Shows that encrypting only sensitive ROIs can preserve exact outputs while locality-preserving architectures obtain order-of-magnitude homomorphic-evaluation speedups, whereas early global mixing removes the benefit. This is valuable architectural efficiency evidence, but the abstract presents conditional rather than a single deployment-wide benchmark, so it is retained as high-value watch.

tracking_records.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions

It is strong edge-runtime evidence, though the workload is network control rather than AI-model serving itself.

tracking_records.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents

Strong evidence that runtime scaffolding and model adaptation must be co-designed, but the abstract does not provide a clean latency/token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watchlist.
